items.title: 761st Tank Battalion
items.description: The first Black armored unit to see combat in World War II, nicknamed 'Black Panthers,' who fought with distinction across Europe.

quiz.q: What was the nickname of the 761st Tank Battalion?
quiz.explanation: The 761st Tank Battalion was nicknamed the 'Black Panthers' and adopted the motto 'Come Out Fighting.'

quiz.q: In which war did the 761st Tank Battalion serve?
quiz.explanation: The 761st fought in World War II, becoming the first Black armored unit to see combat in that war.

quiz.q: What made the 761st Tank Battalion historically significant?
choices: First Black armored unit in combat
First unit to use jet aircraft
quiz.explanation: They were the first African American armored unit to see combat in World War II.

quiz.q: In which theater of war did the 761st Tank Battalion primarily fight?
quiz.explanation: The 761st fought across Europe, including campaigns in France, Belgium, and Germany.

quiz.q: What honor was eventually awarded to the 761st Tank Battalion decades after WWII?
quiz.explanation: The 761st Tank Battalion was awarded the Presidential Unit Citation in 1978, long after their heroic service.

items.title: Alexander Miles
items.description: Inventor who improved elevator safety in the 1880s by designing automatic doors that greatly reduced accidents.

quiz.q: What did Alexander Miles invent or improve?
quiz.explanation: Alexander Miles invented automatic elevator shaft doors, dramatically improving elevator safety.

quiz.q: Why was Miles's elevator invention important?
choices: It prevented people from falling into shafts
quiz.explanation: Before his invention, elevator shaft doors had to be opened manually, causing deadly accidents.

quiz.q: When did Alexander Miles receive his famous patent?
quiz.explanation: Miles was granted U.S. Patent 371,207 for his elevator door mechanism in 1887.

quiz.q: Alexander Miles is an example of what kind of historical figure?
quiz.explanation: Miles is celebrated as one of the great Black inventors of the 19th century.

quiz.q: Miles's invention is still influential because automatic elevator doors are now what?
quiz.explanation: Automatic elevator doors, based on his concept, are now a universal safety standard in buildings everywhere.

items.title: Althea Gibson
items.description: Tennis trailblazer who in 1956 became the first Black player to win a Grand Slam title, opening doors for generations of athletes.

quiz.q: What sport is Althea Gibson famous for?
quiz.explanation: Althea Gibson was a pioneering tennis champion who broke racial barriers in the sport.

quiz.q: What historic milestone did Althea Gibson achieve in 1956?
choices: First Black player to win a Grand Slam
First woman to play at Wimbledon
quiz.explanation: In 1956 she won the French Open, becoming the first Black player to win a Grand Slam title.

quiz.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Althea Gibson win in total?
quiz.explanation: Gibson won five Grand Slam singles titles between 1956 and 1958.

quiz.q: After tennis, Althea Gibson also competed professionally in which other sport?
quiz.explanation: Gibson became the first Black woman to compete on the LPGA golf tour after retiring from tennis.

quiz.q: Gibson's success inspired which later tennis champion?
quiz.explanation: Both Serena and Venus Williams have cited Althea Gibson as a foundational inspiration for their careers.

items.title: Amiri Baraka
items.description: Poet, playwright, and activist who was a central voice of the Black Arts Movement, using literature to challenge racism and inequality.

quiz.q: Amiri Baraka was primarily known as what?
quiz.explanation: Baraka was a groundbreaking poet, playwright, and political activist.

quiz.q: What cultural movement was Amiri Baraka a central figure in?
quiz.explanation: Baraka was a founding figure of the Black Arts Movement of the 1960s and 70s.

quiz.q: What was the name Amiri Baraka used before changing it in 1967?
quiz.explanation: He was born Everett LeRoi Jones and changed his name to Amiri Baraka after Malcolm X's assassination.

quiz.q: Baraka's work often focused on what themes?
quiz.explanation: His writing powerfully addressed racism, Black identity, and the struggle for justice.

quiz.q: What title did New Jersey give Amiri Baraka in 2002?
quiz.explanation: Baraka was named Poet Laureate of New Jersey in 2002.

items.title: Angela Davis
items.description: Scholar, activist, and author who has been a leading voice in movements for racial justice, prison reform, and women's rights for decades.

quiz.q: Angela Davis is best known as what?
quiz.explanation: Angela Davis is a prominent activist, author, and professor known for her work on racial justice and prison reform.

quiz.q: What major cause has Angela Davis championed throughout her life?
quiz.explanation: She is one of the most recognized voices calling for prison abolition and an end to systemic racism.

quiz.q: Angela Davis ran for Vice President of the United States in which years?
quiz.explanation: She was the Communist Party USA's vice presidential candidate in 1980 and 1984.

quiz.q: At which university did Angela Davis teach for many years?
quiz.explanation: Davis was a professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz for many years.

quiz.q: Davis was placed on the FBI's Most Wanted list in 1970 due to what?
choices: Her connection to a courthouse shooting
quiz.explanation: She was placed on the FBI list due to her alleged connection to a 1970 courthouse shooting; she was later acquitted of all charges.

items.title: Arsenio Hall
items.description: Comedian and TV host who broke barriers as one of the first Black hosts of a major late-night talk show in the late 1980s and 90s.

quiz.q: Arsenio Hall is famous for hosting what type of TV program?
quiz.explanation: The Arsenio Hall Show was a hugely popular late-night talk show that ran from 1989 to 1994.

quiz.q: Why was Arsenio Hall's talk show considered groundbreaking?
choices: He was one of the first Black hosts of a major late-night show
He was the youngest host ever
quiz.explanation: Hall broke racial barriers by becoming one of the first Black hosts of a successful late-night network talk show.

quiz.q: Bill Clinton's famous saxophone performance aired on which show?
quiz.explanation: Presidential candidate Bill Clinton famously played the saxophone on The Arsenio Hall Show in 1992.

quiz.q: What signature audience gesture became associated with The Arsenio Hall Show?
quiz.explanation: The show became known for the audience's 'woof woof woof' fist-pumping chant.

quiz.q: Arsenio Hall also appeared in which famous comedy film alongside Eddie Murphy?
quiz.explanation: Hall co-starred with Eddie Murphy in Coming to America (1988), playing multiple characters.

items.title: Arthur Ashe
items.description: Tennis legend who became the first Black man to win Wimbledon and the US Open, and used his platform to fight apartheid and AIDS awareness.

quiz.q: Arthur Ashe was a champion in what sport?
quiz.explanation: Arthur Ashe was one of the greatest tennis players of his era.

quiz.q: What historic first did Arthur Ashe achieve at Wimbledon in 1975?
choices: First Black man to win Wimbledon singles
quiz.explanation: Ashe became the first Black man to win the Wimbledon singles title in 1975.

quiz.q: Off the court, Arthur Ashe was a strong opponent of what political system?
quiz.explanation: Ashe was a vocal and active opponent of apartheid in South Africa.

quiz.q: In his later years, what disease did Arthur Ashe publicly advocate about?
quiz.explanation: After contracting HIV through a blood transfusion, Ashe became a leading advocate for AIDS awareness.

quiz.q: The main stadium at the US Open tennis tournament is named after whom?
quiz.explanation: Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York is the largest tennis stadium in the world, named in his honor.

items.title: Bernie Mac
items.description: Stand-up comedian and actor from Chicago who rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most beloved comedians of his generation.

quiz.q: Bernie Mac was best known as what?
quiz.explanation: Bernie Mac was a celebrated stand-up comedian and actor known for his bold, fearless style.

quiz.q: Bernie Mac was part of which famous stand-up comedy tour?
quiz.explanation: He was one of the four comedians featured in The Original Kings of Comedy concert film (2000).

quiz.q: Bernie Mac starred in his own sitcom named what?
quiz.explanation: The Bernie Mac Show aired on Fox from 2001 to 2006 and earned him a Golden Globe nomination.

quiz.q: Where was Bernie Mac born and raised?
quiz.explanation: Bernie Mac grew up on the South Side of Chicago, and his Chicago roots were central to his comedy.

quiz.q: Bernie Mac also appeared in which popular Ocean's film series?
quiz.explanation: He played Frank Catton in all three Ocean's films: Eleven, Twelve, and Thirteen.

items.title: Bessie Coleman
items.description: Aviation pioneer who became the first African American woman to earn a pilot's license in 1921, inspiring generations of aviators.

quiz.q: What was Bessie Coleman the first African American woman to achieve?
quiz.explanation: In 1921, Bessie Coleman became the first African American woman to earn an international pilot's license.

quiz.q: Because no U.S. school would accept her, where did Coleman go to learn to fly?
quiz.explanation: Coleman moved to France to attend aviation school because American flight schools refused to admit Black women.

quiz.q: Bessie Coleman became famous for performing what kinds of shows?
quiz.explanation: She became a celebrated barnstormer, performing daring aerial stunts at airshows across the country.

quiz.q: Coleman refused to perform at shows that had what condition?
quiz.explanation: She refused to perform at segregated events, insisting that Black and white audiences have equal access.

quiz.q: What nickname was Bessie Coleman given?
quiz.explanation: Bessie Coleman was affectionately known as 'Queen Bess' by her fans and admirers.

items.title: Beyonce Knowles
items.description: Global music icon, singer, songwriter, and actress who became one of the best-selling music artists of all time and a powerful voice for Black culture.

quiz.q: Beyonce first rose to fame as part of which music group?
quiz.explanation: Beyoncé first became famous as the lead singer of Destiny's Child before launching her solo career.

quiz.q: Beyonce's 2016 visual album celebrated Black womanhood and Southern culture. What was it called?
quiz.explanation: Lemonade (2016) was a groundbreaking visual album exploring Black womanhood, heritage, and identity.

quiz.q: Beyonce holds the record for the most Grammy wins by whom?
quiz.explanation: Beyoncé holds the record for the most Grammy Awards won by any artist in Grammy history.

quiz.q: Beyonce's Coachella 2018 performance was notable for what reason?
choices: First Black woman to headline Coachella
First live stream of a concert
First performance with a marching band
quiz.explanation: She was the first Black woman to headline the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival.

quiz.q: What city is Beyonce originally from?
quiz.explanation: Beyoncé was born and raised in Houston, Texas, and frequently celebrates her Texas roots.

items.title: Billie Holiday
items.description: Jazz and blues vocalist whose deeply emotional voice and courageous song 'Strange Fruit' made her one of the most influential singers in American music history.

quiz.q: Billie Holiday was famous for performing what genre of music?
quiz.explanation: Billie Holiday was one of the greatest jazz and blues vocalists of all time.

quiz.q: What powerful anti-lynching song became Billie Holiday's signature protest song?
quiz.explanation: 'Strange Fruit' (1939) was a haunting protest against racial violence and lynching in the South.

quiz.q: What nickname was Billie Holiday given?
quiz.explanation: Jazz musician Lester Young gave her the nickname 'Lady Day,' which stayed with her throughout her life.

quiz.q: Billie Holiday's vocal style was known for what quality?
quiz.explanation: Her ability to convey raw emotion through phrasing and timing set her apart from any other singer.

quiz.q: Which of these songs did Billie Holiday write herself?
quiz.explanation: Holiday co-wrote 'God Bless the Child' in 1941, and it became one of her most celebrated recordings.

items.title: Bo Jackson
items.description: Considered the greatest multi-sport athlete in history, Bo Jackson was an All-Star in both the NFL and MLB, achieving feats no other athlete has matched.

quiz.q: Bo Jackson is celebrated for being elite in how many professional sports?
quiz.explanation: Bo Jackson was an All-Star in both the NFL (Los Angeles Raiders) and MLB (Kansas City Royals).

quiz.q: What prestigious college football award did Bo Jackson win in 1985?
quiz.explanation: Bo Jackson won the Heisman Trophy in 1985 while playing at Auburn University.

quiz.q: Bo Jackson became a pop culture icon through advertisements for which company?
quiz.explanation: The 'Bo Knows' Nike campaign made him one of the most recognizable athletes in advertising history.

quiz.q: A hip injury forced Bo Jackson to retire from which sport first?
quiz.explanation: A hip injury suffered in a 1991 NFL playoff game ended his football career, though he returned briefly to baseball.

quiz.q: Bo Jackson hit one of the longest home runs in All-Star Game history in what year?
quiz.explanation: Jackson led off the 1989 MLB All-Star Game with a massive home run and was named the game's MVP.

items.title: Booker T. Washington
items.description: Born into slavery, Booker T. Washington rose to become one of the most influential educators and leaders of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

quiz.q: Booker T. Washington founded which famous institution?
quiz.explanation: He founded the Tuskegee Normal and Industrial Institute in Alabama in 1881, now Tuskegee University.

quiz.q: Booker T. Washington was born into what condition?
quiz.explanation: Washington was born enslaved in Virginia around 1856, and educated himself after emancipation.

quiz.q: Washington's famous 1895 speech encouraging Black economic self-reliance was called what?
quiz.explanation: The Atlanta Compromise speech argued for Black economic progress through vocational education.

quiz.q: Booker T. Washington was the first Black American to dine with a U.S. president at the White House. Who was that president?
quiz.explanation: President Theodore Roosevelt invited Washington to dinner at the White House in 1901, a historic and controversial event.

quiz.q: What was the title of Booker T. Washington's famous autobiography?
quiz.explanation: 'Up From Slavery' (1901) is Washington's celebrated autobiography describing his journey from enslaved child to national leader.

items.title: Cab Calloway
items.description: Flamboyant jazz singer and bandleader of the Harlem Renaissance era, known for his scat singing, energetic performances, and the signature song 'Minnie the Moocher.'

quiz.q: Cab Calloway was famous as a jazz singer and what else?
quiz.explanation: Calloway was both a celebrated vocalist and bandleader who led one of the most popular big bands of the era.

quiz.q: What was Cab Calloway's most famous song?
quiz.explanation: 'Minnie the Moocher' (1931) became his signature song, famous for its call-and-response 'hi-de-hi-de-hi-de-ho' chorus.

quiz.q: Cab Calloway frequently performed at which famous Harlem venue?
quiz.explanation: Calloway was a star attraction at the legendary Cotton Club in Harlem during the 1930s.

quiz.q: Cab Calloway was known for his use of what vocal technique?
quiz.explanation: His energetic scat singing and nonsense syllables were a trademark of his wild, joyful performances.

quiz.q: In the 1980 film Blues Brothers, which character did Cab Calloway play?
quiz.explanation: Calloway played Curtis, the boys' guardian, in The Blues Brothers (1980), introducing him to a new generation.

items.title: Candace Parker
items.description: WNBA superstar and two-time champion widely regarded as one of the greatest women's basketball players of all time.

quiz.q: Candace Parker is celebrated for her achievements in what sport?
quiz.explanation: Candace Parker is one of the greatest players in WNBA history.

quiz.q: Which WNBA teams did Candace Parker win championships with?
choices: Los Angeles Sparks and Chicago Sky
quiz.explanation: Parker won WNBA titles with the Los Angeles Sparks (2016) and Chicago Sky (2021).

quiz.q: Where did Candace Parker play her dominant college career?
quiz.explanation: Parker played for the Tennessee Lady Vols, winning two NCAA championships under coach Pat Summitt.

quiz.q: Candace Parker was the first woman to do what in an NBA Slam Dunk Contest-style event?
choices: Score 50 points in a college game
quiz.explanation: Parker became the first woman to dunk in NCAA Tournament play during her time at Tennessee.

quiz.q: Candace Parker has also won how many Olympic gold medals with Team USA?
quiz.explanation: Parker won Olympic gold medals with the U.S. women's basketball team in 2008 and 2012.

items.title: Carter G Woodson
items.description: Historian, author, and educator known as the 'Father of Black History' who founded Negro History Week, which became Black History Month.

quiz.q: Carter G. Woodson is known by what honorary title?
quiz.explanation: Woodson is called the 'Father of Black History' for his pioneering work documenting African American history.

quiz.q: What observance did Carter G. Woodson create in 1926?
quiz.explanation: Woodson founded Negro History Week in 1926, which was later expanded to Black History Month in 1976.

quiz.q: What organization did Carter G. Woodson found to study Black history?
choices: Association for the Study of African American Life and History
quiz.explanation: He founded the Association for the Study of Negro Life and History (now ASALH) in 1915.

quiz.q: Carter G. Woodson was only the second African American to earn a PhD from which university?
quiz.explanation: Woodson earned his doctorate from Harvard University in 1912, only the second African American to do so.

quiz.q: What was the title of Carter G. Woodson's most famous book?
quiz.explanation: 'The Mis-Education of the Negro' (1933) argued that Black Americans were being taught to devalue their own heritage.

items.title: Cedric Kyles
items.description: Comedian and actor known professionally as Cedric the Entertainer, celebrated for his work on The Steve Harvey Show, Kings of Comedy, and barbershop films.

quiz.q: Cedric Kyles is better known by what stage name?
quiz.explanation: He performs under the name Cedric the Entertainer, a name that captures his larger-than-life comedic presence.

quiz.q: Cedric the Entertainer was part of which famous comedy tour?
quiz.explanation: He was one of the four comedians featured in The Original Kings of Comedy (2000), directed by Spike Lee.

quiz.q: On The Steve Harvey Show, Cedric the Entertainer played what character?
quiz.explanation: He played Cedric Jackie Robinson, Steve Harvey's best friend, on the WB sitcom from 1996 to 2002.

quiz.q: Cedric the Entertainer starred in which popular barbershop film series?
quiz.explanation: He played the scene-stealing Eddie in the Barbershop film franchise starting in 2002.

quiz.q: Cedric the Entertainer has hosted which major awards ceremony multiple times?
quiz.explanation: He has hosted the BET Awards multiple times and is known for his energetic, crowd-pleasing hosting style.

items.title: Chadwick Boseman
items.description: Actor who inspired millions by portraying iconic Black figures including Jackie Robinson, James Brown, and the Marvel superhero Black Panther.

quiz.q: Chadwick Boseman is most celebrated for playing which Marvel superhero?
quiz.explanation: Boseman portrayed T'Challa, the Black Panther, beginning with Captain America: Civil War (2016) and the landmark Black Panther (2018).

quiz.q: In which 2013 film did Chadwick Boseman portray baseball legend Jackie Robinson?
quiz.explanation: Boseman delivered a celebrated performance as Jackie Robinson in the biopic 42 (2013).

quiz.q: Black Panther (2018) was historically significant because it was what?
choices: First major superhero film with a nearly all-Black cast
First superhero film directed by a Black director
quiz.explanation: Black Panther was the first major superhero blockbuster featuring a nearly all-Black cast and Black director (Ryan Coogler).

quiz.q: Chadwick Boseman filmed his final movies while privately battling what illness?
quiz.explanation: Boseman was diagnosed with colon cancer in 2016 and continued working until his death in 2020 without making his illness public.

quiz.q: Boseman posthumously won an Academy Award nomination for which film?
quiz.explanation: He received a posthumous Oscar nomination for Best Actor for his role in Ma Rainey's Black Bottom (2020).

items.title: Charles Drew
items.description: Surgeon and medical researcher who revolutionized medicine by developing large-scale blood banks and plasma storage techniques that have saved countless lives.

quiz.q: What life-saving medical innovation is Charles Drew credited with pioneering?
quiz.explanation: Drew developed methods for large-scale blood banking and plasma preservation, saving countless lives.

quiz.q: Drew's blood banking work was especially critical during what event?
quiz.explanation: His techniques were used to create blood banks that supplied British and American forces during World War II.

quiz.q: Charles Drew resigned from the American Red Cross over what injustice?
quiz.explanation: Drew protested the Red Cross policy of segregating blood by race, which had no scientific basis.

quiz.q: Charles Drew earned his medical degree and performed his blood research at which university?
quiz.explanation: Drew completed his landmark research and earned his Doctor of Science in Medicine from Columbia University in 1940.

quiz.q: After his resignation from the Red Cross, Drew became the chief of surgery at which historically Black university?
quiz.explanation: Drew became chief of surgery at Howard University Hospital, where he trained generations of Black surgeons.

items.title: Charles Woodson
items.description: Pro Football Hall of Fame cornerback and the only primarily defensive player to win the Heisman Trophy, known for his playmaking on both sides of the ball.

quiz.q: What position did Charles Woodson play in the NFL?
quiz.explanation: Woodson was one of the greatest cornerbacks in NFL history, known for his lockdown coverage and big plays.

quiz.q: Charles Woodson is historically unique because he is the only primarily defensive player to win what award?
quiz.explanation: Woodson won the 1997 Heisman Trophy at Michigan, the only primarily defensive player ever to win the award.

quiz.q: Charles Woodson won a Super Bowl championship with which NFL team?
quiz.explanation: Woodson won Super Bowl XLV with the Green Bay Packers following the 2010 season.

quiz.q: Charles Woodson was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year in which season?
quiz.explanation: Woodson won the NFL Defensive Player of the Year award in 2009 while with the Green Bay Packers.

quiz.q: After football, Charles Woodson became co-owner and brand ambassador for what kind of business?
quiz.explanation: Woodson co-founded the INTERCEPT Wines brand and has become a prominent figure in the wine industry.

items.title: Cicely Tyson
items.description: Legendary actress whose six-decade career broke barriers for Black women in Hollywood and television, earning her an Honorary Academy Award and the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

quiz.q: Cicely Tyson was celebrated in which field?
quiz.explanation: Tyson was one of the most acclaimed actresses in American history, with a career spanning six decades.

quiz.q: Cicely Tyson won an Emmy for her role in which landmark 1974 TV film?
choices: The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman
quiz.explanation: Her portrayal of a 110-year-old formerly enslaved woman in The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman earned her two Emmy Awards.

quiz.q: Tyson received an Honorary Academy Award in 2018 recognizing what?
quiz.explanation: She was awarded an Honorary Oscar in 2018 in recognition of her extraordinary body of work over six decades.

quiz.q: Cicely Tyson was known for carefully choosing roles that did what?
quiz.explanation: Tyson was selective about roles, consistently choosing parts that portrayed Black women with depth and dignity.

quiz.q: Cicely Tyson published her memoir just two days before her death in 2021. What was it called?
quiz.explanation: Her memoir Just As I Am was published on January 26, 2021, two days before she passed away at age 96.

items.title: Dave Chappelle
items.description: Stand-up comedian and writer widely considered one of the greatest comedians of all time, famous for Chappelle's Show and his incisive commentary on race in America.

quiz.q: Dave Chappelle is best known as what type of performer?
quiz.explanation: Chappelle is widely regarded as one of the greatest stand-up comedians in history.

quiz.q: What hugely popular sketch comedy show did Dave Chappelle create for Comedy Central?
quiz.explanation: Chappelle's Show ran from 2003 to 2006 and became one of the best-selling TV DVD releases of all time.

quiz.q: Dave Chappelle famously walked away from what at the height of his fame?
quiz.explanation: In 2005 he walked away from a $50 million deal to continue Chappelle's Show, citing creative and personal conflicts.

quiz.q: Dave Chappelle won multiple Grammy Awards for what?
quiz.explanation: He has won multiple Grammy Awards for Best Comedy Album for his Netflix stand-up specials.

quiz.q: Chappelle's comedy is especially known for addressing what topic?
quiz.explanation: His comedy brilliantly and boldly tackles the complexities of race, identity, and American culture.

items.title: Denzel Washington
items.description: Two-time Academy Award-winning actor and filmmaker considered one of the greatest actors of his generation, known for commanding performances across dramatic films.

quiz.q: How many Academy Awards has Denzel Washington won?
quiz.explanation: Washington has won two Oscars: Best Supporting Actor for Glory (1990) and Best Actor for Training Day (2002).

quiz.q: Denzel Washington won his first Oscar for which film?
quiz.explanation: He won Best Supporting Actor for his role as Private Trip in Glory (1989).

quiz.q: Denzel Washington famously portrayed which civil rights leader in a 1992 biopic?
quiz.explanation: His portrayal of Malcolm X in Spike Lee's 1992 film is widely considered one of the greatest performances in cinema history.

quiz.q: Washington has had a long relationship with which playwright's work, appearing in Broadway revivals and film adaptations?
quiz.explanation: Washington has championed August Wilson's work on stage and screen, including Fences (2016) which he directed and starred in.

quiz.q: Denzel Washington is the second Black man in history to win the Best Actor Oscar. Who was the first?
quiz.explanation: Sidney Poitier won Best Actor in 1964 for Lilies of the Field; Denzel Washington became the second Black man to win the award in 2002.

items.title: Diana Ross
items.description: Music icon who led The Supremes to become Motown's most successful group before launching a legendary solo career spanning decades.

quiz.q: Diana Ross first became famous as the lead singer of which group?
quiz.explanation: Ross led The Supremes to become Motown's best-selling group of all time, with 12 number-one singles.

quiz.q: The Supremes were the flagship act of which legendary record label?
quiz.explanation: The Supremes were the crown jewel of Berry Gordy's Motown Records in Detroit.

quiz.q: Diana Ross received an Academy Award nomination for playing which jazz legend?
quiz.explanation: Ross received a Best Actress Oscar nomination for her portrayal of Billie Holiday in Lady Sings the Blues (1972).

quiz.q: Diana Ross performed a famous free outdoor concert in New York's Central Park during what weather event?
quiz.explanation: Her 1983 Central Park concert was interrupted by a severe thunderstorm, but she returned the next night to complete the show.

quiz.q: The Guinness Book of World Records recognized Diana Ross as what?
choices: Most successful female music artist of all time
First woman to have 12 number-one hits
quiz.explanation: Guinness recognized her as the most successful female music artist of all time based on total records sold.

items.title: Dizzy Gillespie
items.description: Trumpet virtuoso and co-creator of bebop jazz who revolutionized modern music and became a global ambassador for jazz.

quiz.q: Dizzy Gillespie was a master of which instrument?
quiz.explanation: Gillespie was one of the greatest trumpet players in history, known for his speed, range, and innovation.

quiz.q: Dizzy Gillespie is credited as a co-creator of which revolutionary jazz style?
quiz.explanation: Along with Charlie Parker, Gillespie co-created bebop in the 1940s, fundamentally changing jazz forever.

quiz.q: What was distinctive about Dizzy Gillespie's trumpet?
choices: It was double the normal size
It was made of silver instead of brass
quiz.explanation: His trademark trumpet had a bell bent upward at a 45-degree angle, which he claimed improved the sound directed at him on stage.

quiz.q: Dizzy Gillespie also helped popularize which Latin music fusion style?
quiz.explanation: Gillespie merged jazz with Afro-Cuban rhythms, helping create Afro-Cuban jazz and later Latin jazz.

quiz.q: The U.S. State Department sent Dizzy Gillespie on international tours in the 1950s for what purpose?
quiz.explanation: The State Department used his international tours as cultural diplomacy during the Cold War, earning him the nickname 'Jazz Ambassador.'

items.title: Donald Glover Jr.
items.description: Multi-hyphenate creative force known as Childish Gambino in music, celebrated for acting, writing, directing, and producing across television, film, and music.

quiz.q: Donald Glover performs music under what stage name?
quiz.explanation: He records and performs music as Childish Gambino, a name generated from a Wu-Tang Clan name generator.

quiz.q: Donald Glover created and starred in which acclaimed FX television series?
quiz.explanation: Atlanta (2016–2022) was created by and starred Glover, winning multiple Emmy and Golden Globe awards.

quiz.q: Childish Gambino's music video for 'This Is America' became a cultural moment because it addressed what?
quiz.explanation: The 2018 video's striking imagery depicting gun violence and the treatment of Black Americans sparked widespread cultural conversation.

quiz.q: Donald Glover played which Star Wars character in a 2018 film?
quiz.explanation: He played a young Lando Calrissian in Solo: A Star Wars Story (2018).

quiz.q: Donald Glover began his career as a writer for which television comedy?
quiz.explanation: Glover got his first big break writing for Tina Fey's 30 Rock while still in college at New York University.

items.title: Dorothy Dandridge
items.description: Actress and singer who in 1955 became the first African American woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress, breaking barriers in Hollywood.

quiz.q: Dorothy Dandridge made history in 1955 by becoming what?
choices: First Black woman nominated for Best Actress Oscar
First Black woman to star in a Hollywood film
First Black woman to win a Golden Globe
First Black woman to appear on a magazine cover
quiz.explanation: She received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for Carmen Jones (1954), a historic first for a Black woman.

quiz.q: Dorothy Dandridge starred in which 1954 musical film that earned her an Oscar nomination?
quiz.explanation: Her electrifying performance in Carmen Jones (1954) made her an international star and earned the Oscar nomination.

quiz.q: Despite her talent, Dandridge faced what significant obstacle in Hollywood?
quiz.explanation: Racial segregation severely limited the roles available to her, and she was often denied opportunities given to white actresses of equal fame.

quiz.q: Dandridge also appeared on the cover of which major magazine, another historic first?
quiz.explanation: She became the first Black woman on the cover of Life magazine in 1954.

quiz.q: Which actress portrayed Dorothy Dandridge in a celebrated 1999 HBO biopic?
quiz.explanation: Halle Berry won an Emmy and Golden Globe for portraying Dorothy Dandridge in Introducing Dorothy Dandridge (1999).

items.title: Eddie Murphy
items.description: Comedy legend who rose to fame on Saturday Night Live before becoming one of the highest-grossing actors in Hollywood history.

quiz.q: Eddie Murphy first became a national star on which television show?
quiz.explanation: Murphy joined Saturday Night Live at 19 years old in 1980 and quickly became the show's biggest star.

quiz.q: Which 1984 action-comedy film made Eddie Murphy one of Hollywood's biggest stars?
quiz.explanation: Beverly Hills Cop (1984) was the highest-grossing film of that year and launched Murphy into superstardom.

quiz.q: In the animated film Shrek, Eddie Murphy voices which character?
quiz.explanation: Murphy's voice performance as Donkey in the Shrek franchise is one of the most beloved animated performances ever.

quiz.q: Eddie Murphy's stand-up specials Delirious and Raw are considered what?
choices: Among the greatest stand-up specials ever made
quiz.explanation: Delirious (1983) and Raw (1987) are both considered among the greatest stand-up comedy specials in history.

quiz.q: Murphy received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor for which film?
quiz.explanation: He received a Best Supporting Actor Oscar nomination for his performance as James 'Thunder' Early in Dreamgirls (2006).

items.title: Edmonia Lewis
items.description: Groundbreaking sculptor of the 19th century who was the first professionally successful African American and Native American visual artist in the United States.

quiz.q: Edmonia Lewis was celebrated for her work in what art form?
quiz.explanation: Lewis was a Neoclassical sculptor who worked primarily in marble and achieved international recognition.

quiz.q: Edmonia Lewis was notable for her mixed heritage. What were her backgrounds?
choices: African American and Chippewa Native American
quiz.explanation: Lewis was of African American and Chippewa (Ojibwe) Native American descent, and her art often reflected both heritages.

quiz.q: Edmonia Lewis created a famous marble sculpture depicting which biblical story?
quiz.explanation: Forever Free (1867) depicted an enslaved man and woman being freed, celebrating the end of slavery.

quiz.q: Lewis moved to which European city to pursue her sculpting career?
quiz.explanation: She moved to Rome in 1866, where she could access marble and training unavailable to Black women in America.

quiz.q: President Ulysses S. Grant sat for a portrait sculpture by which artist?
quiz.explanation: Lewis sculpted a portrait bust of President Grant, a remarkable achievement for a Black woman artist in that era.

items.title: Eldrick Tont Woods
items.description: Known worldwide as Tiger Woods, he transformed professional golf and became one of the greatest athletes of all time with 15 major championships.

quiz.q: Eldrick Tont Woods is known worldwide by what nickname?
quiz.explanation: His father nicknamed him Tiger after a Vietnamese soldier friend, and the name stuck throughout his legendary career.

quiz.q: How many major golf championships has Tiger Woods won?
quiz.explanation: Woods has won 15 major championships, second only to Jack Nicklaus's record of 18.

quiz.q: Tiger Woods won his first Masters Tournament in 1997 by a record margin. How old was he?
quiz.explanation: Woods won the 1997 Masters at age 21, becoming the youngest Masters champion ever at the time.

quiz.q: Tiger Woods achieved what is known as the 'Tiger Slam' by holding all four major titles at once in which years?
quiz.explanation: Woods held all four major championship titles simultaneously from 2000 to 2001, an unprecedented feat.

quiz.q: Tiger Woods won the 2019 Masters after years of injury and personal struggles. Why was this victory especially meaningful?
choices: He had not won a major in 11 years
It was his first Masters title
He played with a broken leg
He was the oldest Masters winner ever
quiz.explanation: His 2019 Masters win came after 11 years without a major championship, multiple back surgeries, and a remarkable personal comeback.

items.title: Elijah McCoy
items.description: Prolific inventor who held over 50 patents, best known for his automatic lubrication device for steam engines that inspired the phrase 'the real McCoy.'

quiz.q: Elijah McCoy is best known for inventing a device that did what?
quiz.explanation: McCoy invented an automatic lubricator for steam engines, allowing trains to run without stopping to be oiled by hand.

quiz.q: Approximately how many patents did Elijah McCoy hold during his lifetime?
quiz.explanation: McCoy was granted more than 50 patents over his career, making him one of the most prolific inventors of his era.

quiz.q: The common phrase 'the real McCoy' is believed by many to originate from what?
choices: Engineers insisting on genuine McCoy lubricators
A famous court case about his name
quiz.explanation: Engineers and buyers would insist on 'the real McCoy' to distinguish his superior lubricators from inferior imitations.

quiz.q: Despite his many inventions, McCoy faced what significant barrier in his career?
choices: Racial discrimination limiting his recognition and opportunity
quiz.explanation: Because of racial discrimination, McCoy was often denied the recognition and financial rewards his inventions deserved.

quiz.q: Elijah McCoy was born to parents who had escaped slavery via which route?
quiz.explanation: His parents escaped slavery in Kentucky via the Underground Railroad and settled in Ontario, Canada, where Elijah was born.

items.title: Ella Baker
items.description: Tireless civil rights organizer who worked behind the scenes for decades, mentoring young activists and helping found the SNCC, shaping the entire civil rights movement.

quiz.q: Ella Baker is best remembered as what type of figure in the civil rights movement?
quiz.explanation: Baker believed in empowering ordinary people and worked tirelessly behind the scenes as an organizer and mentor.

quiz.q: Ella Baker helped found which important civil rights organization in 1960?
quiz.explanation: Baker played a key role in founding the SNCC in 1960, which became a driving force of the civil rights movement.

quiz.q: Ella Baker also worked for many years as a field organizer and director for which organization?
quiz.explanation: Baker worked for the NAACP for years, traveling across the South to build chapters and organize communities.

quiz.q: Baker was known for her belief that the movement should be led by whom?
quiz.explanation: She championed group-centered leadership and believed young people and local communities should drive change rather than charismatic individual leaders.

quiz.q: Ella Baker's famous quote 'We who believe in freedom cannot rest' became the refrain of a song honoring her written by whom?
quiz.explanation: Bernice Johnson Reagon wrote 'Ella's Song' for Sweet Honey in the Rock, built around Baker's powerful words.

items.title: Ella Fitzgerald
items.description: Known as the 'First Lady of Song,' Ella Fitzgerald's flawless voice, impeccable timing, and extraordinary scat singing made her the most celebrated jazz vocalist of all time.

quiz.q: What honorary title was Ella Fitzgerald given recognizing her place in music?
quiz.explanation: Ella Fitzgerald was widely known as the 'First Lady of Song' for her unmatched vocal purity and range.

quiz.q: How many Grammy Awards did Ella Fitzgerald win during her career?
quiz.explanation: Fitzgerald won 13 Grammy Awards over her career, including the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.

quiz.q: Ella Fitzgerald is especially celebrated for her recordings of 'songbook' albums dedicated to which composers?
choices: Cole Porter, George Gershwin, and others
Duke Ellington and Louis Armstrong only
quiz.explanation: Her series of 'Songbook' albums covering Cole Porter, George Gershwin, Irving Berlin, and others are considered her masterworks.

quiz.q: Ella Fitzgerald got her big break when she won an amateur night contest at which famous venue?
quiz.explanation: She won Amateur Night at the Apollo Theater in 1934 at age 17, launching her extraordinary career.

quiz.q: Fitzgerald collaborated most famously with which jazz impresario and bandleader?
quiz.explanation: Chick Webb gave Fitzgerald her first big break and she became the featured vocalist with his orchestra.

items.title: Ethel Hedgeman Lyle
items.description: Educator and visionary leader who co-founded Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority in 1908, the first Greek-letter sorority established by and for African American women.

quiz.q: Ethel Hedgeman Lyle is celebrated for co-founding which organization in 1908?
quiz.explanation: Lyle was the chief architect behind founding Alpha Kappa Alpha (AKA) at Howard University in 1908.

quiz.q: Alpha Kappa Alpha was historically significant as what?
choices: First Greek-letter sorority for Black women
First sorority at a Northern university
First sorority open to all races
quiz.explanation: AKA was the first Greek-letter organization established by and for African American women in the United States.

quiz.q: At which university was Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority founded?
quiz.explanation: AKA was founded at Howard University in Washington, D.C., one of America's most prominent HBCUs.

quiz.q: What was Ethel Hedgeman Lyle's profession besides sorority founder?
quiz.explanation: Lyle was a dedicated educator who spent her career in schools and mentoring young women.

quiz.q: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority today is known for its motto and commitment to what?
quiz.explanation: AKA's motto is 'By the Dawn's Early Light' and its mission centers on service to all mankind and the advancement of Black women.

items.title: Faith Ringgold
items.description: Artist, author, and activist celebrated for her story quilts that blend painting, quilted fabric, and narrative to explore the Black American experience.

quiz.q: Faith Ringgold is best known for what unique art form?
quiz.explanation: Ringgold pioneered the story quilt, combining painted narrative scenes with quilted fabric borders to tell stories.

quiz.q: What is the title of Faith Ringgold's most famous children's book, adapted from one of her quilts?
quiz.explanation: Tar Beach (1991) was adapted from her story quilt and won the Caldecott Honor, becoming a beloved children's classic.

quiz.q: Faith Ringgold's art frequently explores what themes?
choices: Race, gender, and the Black American experience
quiz.explanation: Her work powerfully addresses racism, sexism, and the richness and struggles of Black American life.

quiz.q: Ringgold was also active in which movements beyond art?
quiz.explanation: She was an active participant in both the civil rights and feminist movements, protesting discrimination in the art world.

quiz.q: Faith Ringgold taught art for many years at which university?
quiz.explanation: Ringgold was a professor of art at the University of California, San Diego for many years.

items.title: Fannie Lou Hamer
items.description: Sharecropper turned fearless civil rights leader whose powerful voice and courage in the face of brutal violence helped transform voting rights in America.

quiz.q: Fannie Lou Hamer was a powerful leader in the fight for what specific right?
quiz.explanation: Hamer dedicated her life to securing voting rights for Black Americans, particularly in Mississippi.

quiz.q: Before becoming a civil rights activist, Fannie Lou Hamer worked as what?
quiz.explanation: Hamer was a sharecropper on a Mississippi plantation until she tried to register to vote in 1962 and was evicted from her home.

quiz.q: Hamer's powerful 1964 testimony before the Democratic National Committee was about what?
choices: Violent repression of Black voters in Mississippi
Prison conditions for civil rights workers
quiz.explanation: Her televised testimony described the brutal beatings and intimidation faced by Black Mississippians trying to register to vote.

quiz.q: Fannie Lou Hamer co-founded which alternative political party to challenge Mississippi's all-white delegation?
quiz.explanation: She co-founded the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party (MFDP) in 1964 to challenge the exclusion of Black voters.

quiz.q: What famous phrase is Fannie Lou Hamer known for saying about being tired of oppression?
choices: I'm sick and tired of being sick and tired
quiz.explanation: Her famous declaration 'I'm sick and tired of being sick and tired' became one of the most powerful rallying cries of the civil rights era.

items.title: Frederick Douglass
items.description: Escaped enslaved man who became the 19th century's most powerful abolitionist, orator, writer, and statesman, reshaping the national conversation on freedom and equality.

quiz.q: Frederick Douglass is best known as a leading figure in which movement?
quiz.explanation: Douglass was the most prominent Black abolitionist of the 19th century, fighting tirelessly for the end of slavery.

quiz.q: What is the title of Frederick Douglass's celebrated autobiography published in 1845?
choices: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass
Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl
quiz.explanation: His Narrative (1845) was a landmark memoir that exposed the horrors of slavery and became a bestseller internationally.

quiz.q: Douglass escaped slavery in 1838 by disguising himself how?
quiz.explanation: He escaped by borrowing a free Black sailor's identification papers and traveling north by train and steamboat.

quiz.q: Frederick Douglass met with President Abraham Lincoln to advocate for what?
choices: The enlistment and equal treatment of Black soldiers
quiz.explanation: Douglass met with Lincoln multiple times, most notably to push for the enlistment and equal pay of Black Union soldiers.

quiz.q: Douglass published an influential abolitionist newspaper called what?
quiz.explanation: He founded and published The North Star beginning in 1847, a powerful anti-slavery newspaper based in Rochester, New York.

items.title: Frederick McKinley
items.description: Inventor and entrepreneur who created the first electric trolley system and over 100 inventions, becoming one of the most prolific Black inventors of the early 20th century.

quiz.q: Frederick McKinley Jones is best known for inventing what technology that transformed an entire industry?
quiz.explanation: Jones co-invented the first practical portable refrigeration system for long-haul trucks, revolutionizing the food transport industry.

quiz.q: Frederick McKinley Jones co-founded which company to manufacture his refrigeration units?
quiz.explanation: Jones and Joseph Numero co-founded the U.S. Thermo Control Company, later known as Thermo King.

quiz.q: Jones's refrigeration technology was especially critical during which world event?
quiz.explanation: His portable refrigeration units were used by the U.S. military in WWII to preserve blood, medicine, and food.

quiz.q: How many patents did Frederick McKinley Jones hold in his lifetime?
quiz.explanation: Jones held more than 60 patents covering refrigeration, sound equipment, and other innovations.

quiz.q: Frederick McKinley Jones was posthumously awarded which presidential honor in 1991?
quiz.explanation: President George H.W. Bush posthumously awarded Jones the National Medal of Technology in 1991.

items.title: Garrett Morgan
items.description: Inventor and businessman who created the three-position traffic signal and the safety hood, a forerunner of the modern gas mask, saving countless lives.

quiz.q: Garrett Morgan is credited with inventing an improved version of which everyday safety device?
quiz.explanation: Morgan invented the three-position traffic signal in 1923, adding a warning position between stop and go that is the basis for modern signals.

quiz.q: Garrett Morgan also invented a safety device to protect people from smoke and gas. What was it?
quiz.explanation: His 1914 'safety hood' was a forerunner of the modern gas mask, designed to allow wearers to breathe safely in smoky environments.

quiz.q: Morgan's safety hood was used heroically in 1916 to rescue workers trapped where?
choices: A tunnel explosion under Lake Erie
quiz.explanation: Morgan personally used his safety hood to rescue workers trapped after an explosion in a tunnel beneath Lake Erie in Cleveland.

quiz.q: To sell his safety hood in the South, Morgan sometimes had to disguise himself. Why?
choices: Racial prejudice would have prevented sales if customers knew he was Black
quiz.explanation: Because of racism, Morgan sometimes posed as a Native American man named 'Big Chief Mason' to demonstrate and sell his device in the South.

quiz.q: Garrett Morgan also founded Cleveland's first Black-owned newspaper. What was it called?
quiz.explanation: Morgan founded the Cleveland Call newspaper in 1920, which became an important voice for the Black community.

items.title: George Washington Carver
items.description: Agricultural scientist and inventor known as the 'Peanut Man' who revolutionized Southern agriculture and developed hundreds of practical products from peanuts, sweet potatoes, and soybeans.

quiz.q: George Washington Carver is most famous for his research on which crop?
quiz.explanation: Carver developed over 300 products derived from peanuts, earning him the nickname 'the Peanut Man.'

quiz.q: Carver conducted his groundbreaking agricultural research at which institution?
quiz.explanation: He worked at Booker T. Washington's Tuskegee Institute in Alabama for nearly 50 years.

quiz.q: Why did Carver promote peanuts and sweet potatoes to Southern farmers?
choices: To restore soil depleted by cotton farming
Because they were easier to harvest
quiz.explanation: He taught farmers to rotate crops with peanuts and sweet potatoes to replenish soil nutrients depleted by years of cotton cultivation.

quiz.q: George Washington Carver was born into what circumstance?
choices: A free Black family in the North
quiz.explanation: Carver was born into slavery around 1864 in Missouri and was orphaned as an infant.

quiz.q: What did Carver famously refuse to do with his many patents and discoveries?
quiz.explanation: Carver refused to patent most of his discoveries, believing his gifts came from God and should be shared freely with humanity.

items.title: Gerald Lawson
items.description: Pioneer video game engineer who designed the Fairchild Channel F, the first home video game console to use interchangeable cartridges, changing gaming forever.

quiz.q: Gerald Lawson is credited with pioneering what technology that shaped modern video gaming?
quiz.explanation: Lawson designed the Fairchild Channel F in 1976, the first console to use swappable ROM cartridges — a concept every modern console still uses.

quiz.q: What was the name of the home video game console Lawson helped design?
quiz.explanation: The Fairchild Channel F (1976) was the world's first programmable ROM cartridge-based video game console.

quiz.q: Before interchangeable cartridges, how were home video games typically sold?
choices: Built into the console with no way to change games
quiz.explanation: Earlier consoles like the Magnavox Odyssey had games built in or used simple overlays — Lawson's cartridge system allowed entirely new games to be loaded.

quiz.q: Lawson worked on the Channel F while employed at which company?
quiz.explanation: Lawson led the engineering team at Fairchild Semiconductor that developed the Channel F console.

quiz.q: Gerald Lawson was notably rare in the early video game industry because he was what?
choices: One of the very few Black engineers in the field
The only woman in the industry
quiz.explanation: Lawson was one of the very few Black engineers working in the early video game industry in Silicon Valley.

items.title: Halle Berry
items.description: Academy Award-winning actress who made history in 2002 as the first and still only Black woman to win the Oscar for Best Actress.

quiz.q: What historic Oscar milestone did Halle Berry achieve in 2002?
choices: First Black woman to win Best Actress
First Black woman nominated for Best Actress
First Black woman to produce an Oscar-winning film
First Black woman to win two Oscars
quiz.explanation: Berry became the first — and still only — Black woman to win the Academy Award for Best Actress, for Monster's Ball (2001).

quiz.q: Halle Berry won her Oscar for which film?
quiz.explanation: Her raw, powerful performance in Monster's Ball (2001) earned her the historic Best Actress Academy Award.

quiz.q: Halle Berry played which iconic spy role in the James Bond franchise?
choices: Nomi in No Time to Die
Wai Lin in Tomorrow Never Dies
Christmas Jones in The World Is Not Enough
quiz.explanation: Berry played NSA agent Jinx alongside Pierce Brosnan's Bond in Die Another Day (2002).

quiz.q: Halle Berry played which Marvel character in the X-Men film series?
quiz.explanation: Berry played Ororo Munroe, also known as Storm, across multiple X-Men films beginning in 2000.

quiz.q: Before acting, Halle Berry competed in which field?
quiz.explanation: Berry competed in beauty pageants, finishing as first runner-up in the Miss USA pageant and representing the U.S. in Miss World in 1986.

items.title: Harriet Tubman
items.description: Escaped enslaved woman who became the most celebrated conductor of the Underground Railroad, leading over 70 people to freedom and later serving as a Union spy.

quiz.q: What nickname was Harriet Tubman given for leading people to freedom?
quiz.explanation: She was called 'Moses' after the biblical figure who led his people out of bondage, because she led so many to freedom.

quiz.q: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery in what year?
quiz.explanation: Tubman escaped from a Maryland plantation in 1849 and made her way north to Philadelphia.

quiz.q: Approximately how many enslaved people did Tubman lead to freedom via the Underground Railroad?
quiz.explanation: Tubman made roughly 13 missions back into slave territory and guided more than 70 people to freedom.

quiz.q: During the Civil War, Harriet Tubman served the Union Army in what roles?
quiz.explanation: Tubman served the Union as a spy, scout, and nurse, and led an armed raid that freed over 700 enslaved people.

quiz.q: Harriet Tubman's image was announced to replace whose face on the U.S. $20 bill?
quiz.explanation: The U.S. Treasury announced plans to place Tubman's image on the $20 bill, replacing President Andrew Jackson.

items.title: Hattie McDaniel
items.description: Actress and singer who in 1940 became the first African American to win an Academy Award, for her role as Mammy in Gone with the Wind.

quiz.q: What historic first did Hattie McDaniel achieve at the 1940 Academy Awards?
choices: First Black person to win an Oscar
First woman to win Best Supporting Actress
First Black person nominated for an Oscar
First Black actress to star in a Hollywood film
quiz.explanation: McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award, taking Best Supporting Actress for Gone with the Wind.

quiz.q: Hattie McDaniel won her Oscar for playing which character in Gone with the Wind?
quiz.explanation: She played Mammy, the house slave and confidante to the O'Hara family, a role she imbued with dignity and power.

quiz.q: Despite winning an Oscar, McDaniel was forced to sit where at the Academy Awards ceremony?
choices: At a segregated table at the back of the room
She was not allowed to attend
quiz.explanation: McDaniel was seated at a segregated table at the back of the Ambassador Hotel ballroom, away from her co-stars.

quiz.q: Hattie McDaniel was also a pioneering figure in radio and television. What show did she star in?
quiz.explanation: She starred in the radio and TV series Beulah from 1947, becoming the first Black American to star in their own TV show.

quiz.q: Some critics within the Black community objected to the roles McDaniel played. How did she respond?
choices: She said she'd rather play a maid than be one
She refused to respond to critics
She only accepted dignified roles after 1940
quiz.explanation: McDaniel famously responded that she would rather play a maid for $700 a week than be one for $7 a week.

items.title: Hazel Scott
items.description: Jazz and classical pianist, singer, and actress who became the first Black American to host her own TV show and refused to perform for segregated audiences.

quiz.q: Hazel Scott made history as the first Black American to do what on television?
quiz.explanation: The Hazel Scott Show (1950) made her the first Black American to host their own television program.

quiz.q: Hazel Scott was celebrated for her ability to perform in what two musical styles?
quiz.explanation: Scott was renowned for her unique ability to blend jazz and classical piano in virtuoso performances.

quiz.q: Hazel Scott was known for refusing to perform for what kind of audiences?
quiz.explanation: She consistently refused to perform before segregated audiences, a courageous stand that cost her bookings and income.

quiz.q: Hazel Scott's TV show was cancelled after she did what?
choices: Testified before the House Un-American Activities Committee
Refused to change her musical style
quiz.explanation: After she testified before HUAC in 1950 and criticized McCarthyism, she was blacklisted and her show was cancelled.

quiz.q: Hazel Scott was married to which prominent Black politician and civil rights advocate?
quiz.explanation: Scott was married to Congressman Adam Clayton Powell Jr. of New York from 1945 to 1960.

items.title: Ice Cube
items.description: Rapper, actor, and filmmaker from South Central Los Angeles who helped pioneer West Coast gangsta rap with N.W.A before building a legendary solo and entertainment career.

quiz.q: Ice Cube first rose to fame as a member of which groundbreaking rap group?
quiz.explanation: Ice Cube was the primary lyricist for N.W.A, the Compton-based group that launched gangsta rap.

quiz.q: Ice Cube's debut solo album, released in 1990, is considered a classic. What was it called?
quiz.explanation: AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted (1990) was a critically acclaimed debut that cemented his status as a solo artist.

quiz.q: Ice Cube co-wrote and starred in which 1995 comedy film set in South Central LA?
quiz.explanation: Friday (1995), which he co-wrote and starred in alongside Chris Tucker, became a beloved comedy classic.

quiz.q: Ice Cube also co-founded which professional basketball league focused on former NBA players?
quiz.explanation: He co-founded the BIG3, a professional 3-on-3 basketball league featuring former NBA players, launched in 2017.

quiz.q: The 2015 N.W.A biopic that Ice Cube helped produce, featuring his son O'Shea Jackson Jr. as him, was called what?
quiz.explanation: Straight Outta Compton (2015) was a critically acclaimed biopic about N.W.A that Ice Cube helped produce.

items.title: Ida B Wells
items.description: Journalist, activist, and co-founder of the NAACP whose fearless investigative reporting on lynching helped expose racial terror in America to the world.

quiz.q: Ida B. Wells is best remembered for her courageous reporting on what crime?
quiz.explanation: Wells conducted groundbreaking investigative journalism documenting the epidemic of lynching in the American South.

quiz.q: Ida B. Wells was a co-founder of which major civil rights organization?
quiz.explanation: Wells was one of the co-founders of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in 1909.

quiz.q: Wells published a landmark anti-lynching pamphlet in 1892 titled what?
choices: Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases
quiz.explanation: Southern Horrors (1892) used meticulous research to debunk myths used to justify lynching and exposed it as racial terrorism.

quiz.q: After her Memphis newspaper office was destroyed in retaliation for her reporting, Wells continued her crusade from where?
quiz.explanation: After a Memphis mob destroyed her newspaper and threatened her life, she relocated to New York and later Chicago, continuing her anti-lynching work.

quiz.q: Ida B. Wells was posthumously awarded a Pulitzer Prize Special Citation in what year?
quiz.explanation: Wells was awarded a posthumous Pulitzer Prize Special Citation in 2020 for her outstanding and courageous reporting.

items.title: Jack Robinson
items.description: Known as Jackie Robinson, he broke Major League Baseball's color barrier in 1947 when he joined the Brooklyn Dodgers, becoming one of the most important figures in American sports history.

quiz.q: Jackie Robinson is celebrated for breaking the color barrier in which sport?
quiz.explanation: Robinson broke MLB's color barrier on April 15, 1947, when he took the field for the Brooklyn Dodgers.

quiz.q: Which MLB team did Jackie Robinson debut with in 1947?
quiz.explanation: Robinson joined the Brooklyn Dodgers, making history as the first Black player in MLB's modern era.

quiz.q: Which Brooklyn Dodgers executive signed Jackie Robinson and championed his entry into MLB?
quiz.explanation: General manager Branch Rickey specifically recruited Robinson, knowing he needed a player with extraordinary strength of character to endure the hatred he would face.

quiz.q: In honor of Jackie Robinson, MLB retired his jersey number league-wide. What was his number?
quiz.explanation: MLB retired number 42 across all teams in 1997, the 50th anniversary of Robinson's debut — the only number retired league-wide.

quiz.q: Before baseball, Jackie Robinson was a multi-sport star athlete at which university?
quiz.explanation: Robinson was the first athlete at UCLA to letter in four sports: baseball, basketball, football, and track.

items.title: James Brown
items.description: The Godfather of Soul whose explosive performances, innovative rhythms, and iconic recordings made him one of the most sampled and influential musicians in history.

quiz.q: James Brown is known by which legendary title?
choices: The Hardest Working Man in Showbiz
quiz.explanation: Brown earned multiple nicknames including 'The Godfather of Soul,' 'Mr. Dynamite,' and 'The Hardest Working Man in Show Business.'

quiz.q: James Brown is considered a founding father of which musical genre?
quiz.explanation: Brown is widely credited as one of the primary creators of funk music through his rhythmic innovations in the late 1960s.

quiz.q: Which James Brown song became an anthem of Black pride during the civil rights era?
choices: Say It Loud — I'm Black and I'm Proud
Papa's Got a Brand New Bag
Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine
quiz.explanation: 'Say It Loud — I'm Black and I'm Proud' (1968) was a powerful declaration of Black identity during the civil rights movement.

quiz.q: James Brown's music has been sampled more than almost any other artist. This makes him hugely influential in which genre?
quiz.explanation: Brown's beats and vocal exclamations are among the most sampled in hip-hop history, making him a foundational influence on the genre.

quiz.q: James Brown famously performed in which U.S. city the night after Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated, helping to prevent riots?
quiz.explanation: Boston's mayor asked Brown to perform on April 5, 1968, broadcasting the concert on TV to keep people home and prevent the riots that erupted in other cities.

items.title: James Cleveland Owens
items.description: Known as Jesse Owens, he delivered one of sport's greatest moments by winning four gold medals at Adolf Hitler's 1936 Berlin Olympics, humiliating Nazi ideology on the world stage.

quiz.q: James Cleveland Owens is best known by what name?
quiz.explanation: He was known as Jesse Owens, a name that came from a teacher mishearing his initials 'J.C.' as 'Jesse.'

quiz.q: How many gold medals did Jesse Owens win at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
quiz.explanation: Owens won four gold medals — in the 100m, 200m, long jump, and 4x100m relay — at the 1936 Berlin Games.

quiz.q: Owens's victories at the 1936 Olympics were especially significant because they contradicted whose ideology?
choices: Adolf Hitler's Nazi ideology of Aryan supremacy
The International Olympic Committee's segregation policies
quiz.explanation: Owens's four gold medals directly challenged Hitler's claims of Aryan racial superiority on the world's biggest stage.

quiz.q: Which other country's athlete did Jesse Owens famously befriend at the 1936 Berlin Games?
quiz.explanation: German competitor Luz Long publicly offered Owens advice during the long jump competition and became his friend, a gesture of humanity that infuriated Nazi officials.

quiz.q: Despite his Olympic triumph, Owens returned home to what treatment in the United States?
choices: Racial discrimination and lack of government recognition
A hero's welcome from President Roosevelt
quiz.explanation: Owens was denied a congratulatory telegram from President Roosevelt and continued to face racial discrimination despite his global fame.

items.title: James Earl Jones
items.description: Legendary actor whose commanding voice and powerful performances spanned Broadway, film, and television for over six decades, from Darth Vader to Mufasa to King Lear.

quiz.q: James Earl Jones is perhaps most recognized worldwide for providing the voice of which villain?
quiz.explanation: Jones provided the iconic deep voice of Darth Vader in the Star Wars franchise beginning in 1977.

quiz.q: James Earl Jones also voiced which beloved character in The Lion King?
quiz.explanation: Jones voiced Mufasa, Simba's wise and noble father, in both the 1994 animated film and the 2019 remake.

quiz.q: James Earl Jones overcame which childhood condition to become one of history's great orators?
quiz.explanation: Jones had such a severe stutter as a child that he barely spoke for years — making his career as one of the world's most celebrated voices all the more remarkable.

quiz.q: Jones received an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for which 1970 film?
quiz.explanation: He was nominated for Best Actor for reprising his Broadway role as boxer Jack Jefferson in The Great White Hope (1970).

quiz.q: James Earl Jones received which lifetime honor from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in 2011?
quiz.explanation: Jones received an Honorary Oscar in 2011 in recognition of his extraordinary body of theatrical and cinematic work.

items.title: Jean Michel Basquiat
items.description: Neo-expressionist painter who rose from New York street art to international art world stardom, creating raw, powerful work exploring race, identity, and capitalism.

quiz.q: Jean-Michel Basquiat began his artistic career doing what on the streets of New York?
choices: Creating public murals for the city
quiz.explanation: Basquiat started as a graffiti writer in Lower Manhattan under the tag SAMO, before transitioning to canvas painting.

quiz.q: Basquiat's painting style is described as what?
quiz.explanation: His raw, energetic style full of text, symbols, and figures is classified as neo-expressionism.

quiz.q: What major themes ran through much of Basquiat's work?
quiz.explanation: His paintings powerfully addressed race, Black identity, capitalism, colonialism, and the human body.

quiz.q: Basquiat became close friends and collaborators with which other famous artist?
quiz.explanation: He developed a celebrated friendship and artistic collaboration with Andy Warhol in the early 1980s.

quiz.q: At what tragically young age did Jean-Michel Basquiat die in 1988?
quiz.explanation: Basquiat died of a heroin overdose in August 1988 at just 27 years old, joining the so-called '27 Club.'

items.title: John Lewis
items.description: Civil rights hero and U.S. Congressman who was beaten on the Edmund Pettus Bridge during Bloody Sunday and spent six decades in 'good trouble' fighting for justice.

quiz.q: John Lewis is famous for his role in the civil rights movement and for serving decades as what?
quiz.explanation: Lewis represented Georgia's 5th congressional district in the U.S. House from 1987 until his death in 2020.

quiz.q: John Lewis was beaten by state troopers on March 7, 1965, during what event?
choices: Bloody Sunday on the Edmund Pettus Bridge
quiz.explanation: Lewis led marchers across the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama, where they were brutally beaten by state troopers in a moment that shocked the nation.

quiz.q: John Lewis was the youngest speaker at the 1963 March on Washington. Who delivered the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech at the same event?
quiz.explanation: Lewis spoke at the 1963 March on Washington at age 23; Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the iconic 'I Have a Dream' speech at the same event.

quiz.q: John Lewis often encouraged people to get into what kind of trouble to fight injustice?
quiz.explanation: Lewis frequently urged people to make 'good trouble, necessary trouble' — his phrase for nonviolent civil disobedience in pursuit of justice.

quiz.q: John Lewis led which civil rights organization as its chairman in the early 1960s?
quiz.explanation: Lewis served as chairman of the SNCC from 1963 to 1966, leading one of the most active civil rights organizations of the era.

items.title: June Jordan
items.description: Poet, essayist, and activist whose work championed racial justice, feminism, and human rights, and whose Poetry for the People program empowered a generation of writers.

quiz.q: June Jordan was celebrated primarily as what type of writer?
quiz.explanation: Jordan was one of the most prolific and celebrated poets and political essayists of the 20th century.

quiz.q: June Jordan founded which influential program at UC Berkeley to teach poetry to underserved communities?
quiz.explanation: She founded Poetry for the People at UC Berkeley in 1991, empowering students from diverse backgrounds to find their poetic voices.

quiz.q: June Jordan's writing consistently addressed which major themes?
quiz.explanation: Her work powerfully explored racial justice, feminism, sexuality, and the rights of oppressed people worldwide.

quiz.q: Jordan was also known for writing what kind of literature for younger readers?
choices: Children's books and young adult fiction
quiz.explanation: Jordan wrote several books for children and young adults, believing in the importance of introducing young readers to justice-centered literature.

quiz.q: June Jordan taught for many years at which prestigious California university?
quiz.explanation: Jordan was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, where she founded Poetry for the People.

items.title: Kamala Harris
items.description: Trailblazing politician who became the first woman, first Black American, and first person of South Asian descent to serve as Vice President of the United States.

quiz.q: Kamala Harris made history in January 2021 by becoming the first what?
choices: Woman and first Black and South Asian American Vice President
Woman elected to the U.S. Senate
Black woman to run for President
Woman to serve as Attorney General of California
quiz.explanation: Harris became the first woman, first Black American, and first person of South Asian descent to serve as Vice President of the United States.

quiz.q: Before becoming Vice President, Kamala Harris served as a U.S. Senator from which state?
quiz.explanation: Harris represented California in the U.S. Senate from 2017 to 2021.

quiz.q: Before her Senate career, Harris served as the Attorney General of which state?
quiz.explanation: She served as California's Attorney General from 2011 to 2017, the first Black and first South Asian person in that role.

quiz.q: Kamala Harris is the daughter of immigrants from which two countries?
quiz.explanation: Her father is from Jamaica and her mother was from India, making her the first person of South Asian descent to hold national office in the U.S.

quiz.q: Kamala Harris attended which historically Black university as an undergraduate?
quiz.explanation: Harris attended Howard University in Washington, D.C., a choice she has said was central to her identity and values.

items.title: Katherine Johnson
items.description: NASA mathematician whose precise orbital calculations were critical to the success of the first U.S. crewed spaceflights, including John Glenn's historic orbit and the Apollo 11 moon landing.

quiz.q: Katherine Johnson worked as a mathematician for which U.S. government agency?
quiz.explanation: Johnson worked at NASA (and its predecessor NACA) from 1953 to 1986, making critical contributions to the space program.

quiz.q: Astronaut John Glenn famously refused to fly his 1962 orbital mission until what?
choices: Katherine Johnson personally verified the computer's calculations
The weather cleared over the Atlantic
quiz.explanation: Glenn so trusted Johnson's mathematical abilities that he insisted she personally check the electronic computer's trajectory calculations before he would board the capsule.

quiz.q: Katherine Johnson's work at NASA was dramatized in which 2016 film?
quiz.explanation: Hidden Figures (2016) told the story of Johnson and her colleagues Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson.

quiz.q: President Barack Obama awarded Katherine Johnson which honor in 2015?
quiz.explanation: Obama awarded Johnson the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015, the nation's highest civilian honor.

quiz.q: Katherine Johnson's calculations were essential to which historic 1969 mission?
quiz.explanation: Her trajectory analysis was critical to the success of the Apollo 11 mission, which landed the first humans on the moon.

items.title: Ketanji Brown Jackson
items.description: Jurist and legal scholar who in 2022 became the first Black woman to serve as an Associate Justice of the United States Supreme Court.

quiz.q: Ketanji Brown Jackson made history in 2022 by becoming the first what?
choices: Black woman on the U.S. Supreme Court
Woman to serve as Chief Justice
Black person on the Supreme Court
quiz.explanation: Justice Jackson became the first Black woman to serve as an Associate Justice of the United States Supreme Court in 2022.

quiz.q: President Biden nominated Ketanji Brown Jackson to replace which retiring Supreme Court Justice?
quiz.explanation: Jackson was nominated to fill the seat vacated by retiring Justice Stephen Breyer.

quiz.q: Ketanji Brown Jackson attended which law school?
quiz.explanation: Jackson earned her undergraduate degree and her law degree from Harvard University.

quiz.q: Before the Supreme Court, Jackson served as a federal judge on which court?
choices: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
U.S. District Court for D.C. only
quiz.explanation: She served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit before her Supreme Court nomination.

quiz.q: Jackson's confirmation hearings in 2022 were notable for what reason beyond her historic nomination?
choices: Intense political questioning that she answered with composure and brilliance
They were the shortest in history
They were conducted entirely in writing
quiz.explanation: Her hearings drew national attention as she faced aggressive questioning with extraordinary poise and legal precision.

items.title: Kevin Hart
items.description: Comedian and actor from Philadelphia who became one of the highest-paid entertainers in the world through relentless work ethic and a global comedy touring career.

quiz.q: Kevin Hart is primarily known as what type of performer?
quiz.explanation: Hart is one of the world's most successful stand-up comedians, who also became a major Hollywood film star.

quiz.q: Kevin Hart grew up in which city?
quiz.explanation: Hart was born and raised in Philadelphia, and his upbringing there features heavily in his comedy.

quiz.q: Kevin Hart's stand-up tour Irresponsible became what kind of record-breaker?
choices: One of the highest-grossing stand-up tours in history
The first stand-up tour broadcast live worldwide
quiz.explanation: Hart's touring has consistently broken box office records, making him one of the highest-grossing touring comedians of all time.

quiz.q: Kevin Hart starred alongside Dwayne Johnson in which popular action-comedy film series?
choices: Ride Along and Think Like a Man
The Wedding Ringer and Get Hard
quiz.explanation: Hart and Johnson teamed up for Central Intelligence (2016) and the Jumanji franchise, becoming one of Hollywood's most popular comedy duos.

quiz.q: Kevin Hart founded which media and entertainment company to expand his business empire?
quiz.explanation: Hart founded HartBeat Productions, which produces films, TV shows, and content across multiple platforms.

items.title: KRS-One
items.description: Rapper and hip-hop philosopher from the South Bronx whose work with Boogie Down Productions and as a solo artist helped define conscious hip-hop and laid the foundation for rap as a cultural force.

quiz.q: KRS-One is known as what within the hip-hop community?
quiz.explanation: KRS-One is known as 'The Teacha' for his philosophical, educational approach to hip-hop and his lectures at universities worldwide.

quiz.q: KRS-One co-founded which groundbreaking hip-hop group in the 1980s?
quiz.explanation: KRS-One and DJ Scott La Rock co-founded Boogie Down Productions (BDP), one of the most influential groups in hip-hop history.

quiz.q: KRS-One's music is categorized as what style of hip-hop?
quiz.explanation: His work is known for its intellectual, political, and Afrocentric themes, making him a central figure in conscious hip-hop.

quiz.q: KRS-One co-founded which hip-hop activism organization in response to violence in the community?
quiz.explanation: After Scott La Rock's murder in 1987, KRS-One co-founded the Stop the Violence Movement, recording the charity single 'Self Destruction.'

quiz.q: KRS-One has famously argued that hip-hop is not just music but what?
choices: A way of life and a philosophical system
quiz.explanation: KRS-One has long maintained that hip-hop is a culture and philosophy — a way of life — not merely an entertainment genre.

items.title: Langston Hughes
items.description: Poet, novelist, and playwright who was the leading voice of the Harlem Renaissance, celebrated for poetry that captured the soul, humor, and struggles of Black American life.

quiz.q: Langston Hughes was the leading literary voice of which major cultural movement?
quiz.explanation: Hughes was the pre-eminent poet of the Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s and 30s, celebrating Black culture and identity.

quiz.q: What was the title of Langston Hughes's first published poem, which brought him national attention?
quiz.explanation: 'The Negro Speaks of Rivers' (1921), published when Hughes was just 19, announced him as a major new voice in American literature.

quiz.q: Hughes's poem 'A Dream Deferred' asks what famous question?
choices: What happens to a dream deferred?
Where do dreams go when they die?
Why do dreams fade in the sun?
Can a dream be born again?
quiz.explanation: The poem opens with 'What happens to a dream deferred?' and explores the consequences of denied hopes and aspirations.

quiz.q: Hughes incorporated the rhythms of what musical genre into his poetry?
quiz.explanation: Hughes pioneered jazz poetry, weaving the rhythms and spirit of jazz and blues into his verse.
