quiz.q: Hughes also created which recurring fictional character who appeared in newspaper columns and books?
quiz.explanation: His beloved character Jesse B. Semple — known as 'Simple' — appeared in newspaper columns and books, offering humorous, sharp commentary on Black life in America.

items.title: Lebron Raymone James Sr.
items.description: NBA superstar widely considered one of the greatest basketball players of all time, who also became a powerful voice for social justice and opened the I PROMISE School in his hometown of Akron.

quiz.q: LeBron James is most celebrated for his career in which sport?
quiz.explanation: LeBron James is widely regarded as one of the greatest NBA players of all time.

quiz.q: LeBron James won NBA championships with how many different teams?
quiz.explanation: James won titles with the Miami Heat (2012, 2013), Cleveland Cavaliers (2016), and Los Angeles Lakers (2020).

quiz.q: LeBron James opened a public school in his hometown to serve at-risk children. What is it called?
quiz.explanation: He opened the I PROMISE School in Akron, Ohio in 2018, providing education and support services for at-risk youth.

quiz.q: LeBron James became the NBA's all-time leading scorer in 2023, surpassing whose record?
quiz.explanation: James surpassed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's long-standing record of 38,387 career points in February 2023.

quiz.q: LeBron James co-founded which media production company with his business partner Maverick Carter?
quiz.explanation: James and Carter co-founded the SpringHill Company, a media and entertainment company that produces films, TV shows, and content.

items.title: Lena Horne
items.description: Singer and actress who broke barriers at MGM as one of the first Black performers with a long-term studio contract, and was a fierce civil rights activist throughout her career.

quiz.q: Lena Horne was celebrated as both a singer and what else?
quiz.explanation: Horne was a celebrated singer and actress who broke barriers in Hollywood and on Broadway.

quiz.q: Lena Horne made history by becoming one of the first Black performers to sign a long-term contract with which major Hollywood studio?
quiz.explanation: Her 1942 MGM contract was a landmark achievement for Black performers in Hollywood.

quiz.q: Despite her MGM contract, Horne's scenes were often filmed so they could be what?
choices: Cut out when shown in Southern states
quiz.explanation: Her scenes were filmed as stand-alone musical numbers so Southern theaters could cut them out without affecting the film's story.

quiz.q: Lena Horne was blacklisted during the McCarthy era for what reason?
choices: Her civil rights activism and associations
Refusing to perform for the military
Her public criticism of a U.S. president
quiz.explanation: Her civil rights activism and association with progressive causes led to her being blacklisted in Hollywood during the 1950s.

quiz.q: Horne's one-woman Broadway show in 1981 earned her which prestigious theater award?
quiz.explanation: Lena Horne: The Lady and Her Music earned her a special Tony Award and ran for 333 performances on Broadway.

items.title: LeVar Burton
items.description: Actor, director, and literacy advocate best known for playing Kunta Kinte in Roots, Geordi La Forge in Star Trek, and hosting the beloved children's program Reading Rainbow for 23 years.

quiz.q: LeVar Burton hosted which beloved educational children's TV program for 23 years?
quiz.explanation: Burton hosted Reading Rainbow from 1983 to 2006, inspiring generations of children to love reading.

quiz.q: LeVar Burton played which enslaved African man in the landmark 1977 miniseries Roots?
quiz.explanation: His portrayal of Kunta Kinte in Roots made Burton a household name at just 19 years old.

quiz.q: In Star Trek: The Next Generation, LeVar Burton played which crew member?
quiz.explanation: Burton played Chief Engineer Geordi La Forge across all seven seasons of The Next Generation and subsequent films.

quiz.q: Reading Rainbow's mission focused on encouraging children to do what?
quiz.explanation: Reading Rainbow's tagline was 'But you don't have to take my word for it' and its mission was to inspire children to read for joy.

quiz.q: Burton successfully crowdfunded a revival of Reading Rainbow in 2014, raising over how much money?
quiz.explanation: His Kickstarter campaign raised over $5 million — the most successful crowdfunding campaign for a film or TV project at the time.

items.title: Lewis Latimer
items.description: Inventor and engineer who improved the incandescent light bulb with a longer-lasting carbon filament and worked closely with both Alexander Graham Bell and Thomas Edison.

quiz.q: Lewis Latimer is most famous for improving which invention?
quiz.explanation: Latimer developed a longer-lasting carbon filament for the light bulb, making electric lighting practical and affordable.

quiz.q: Latimer's improved carbon filament solved what problem with early light bulbs?
quiz.explanation: Early bulbs with bamboo or paper filaments burned out quickly; Latimer's carbon filament lasted much longer, making electric lighting commercially viable.

quiz.q: Lewis Latimer worked as a draftsman for which inventor, helping him patent the telephone?
quiz.explanation: Latimer drew the patent diagrams for Alexander Graham Bell's telephone application, a critical contribution to Bell's historic patent.

quiz.q: Latimer later joined which inventor's team, known as the Edison Pioneers?
quiz.explanation: Latimer joined Thomas Edison's laboratory and became the only Black member of the Edison Pioneers.

quiz.q: Lewis Latimer also supervised the installation of electric streetlights in which major cities?
choices: New York, Philadelphia, Montreal, and London
quiz.explanation: Latimer supervised electric streetlight installation in New York, Philadelphia, Montreal, and London, helping to electrify the world.

items.title: Lisa Gelobter
items.description: Tech pioneer and entrepreneur who played a key role in the development of web animation technology and later used her skills to improve government digital services.

quiz.q: Lisa Gelobter is credited with contributing to the development of which ubiquitous internet technology?
quiz.explanation: Gelobter contributed to the development of Shockwave technology, which was foundational to web animation and the rise of GIFs online.

quiz.q: After her work in tech, Gelobter served in which capacity under President Obama?
choices: Chief Digital Service Officer at the U.S. Department of Education
Director of the U.S. Digital Service
quiz.explanation: She served as Chief Digital Service Officer at the U.S. Department of Education, improving digital services for students and educators.

quiz.q: Lisa Gelobter founded which company focused on making workplaces more equitable?
quiz.explanation: She founded tEQuitable, a platform that provides employees a confidential way to address workplace bias and harassment.

quiz.q: Lisa Gelobter is recognized as a pioneering figure in which industry?
quiz.explanation: She is celebrated as a pioneering Black woman in the technology and software engineering industry.

quiz.q: Gelobter has been a vocal advocate for what cause within the tech industry?
quiz.explanation: She is a prominent advocate for diversity, equity, and inclusion in the technology sector.

items.title: Lonnie Johnson
items.description: NASA engineer and inventor who accidentally invented the Super Soaker water gun while working on a heat pump project, creating one of the best-selling toys of all time.

quiz.q: Lonnie Johnson accidentally invented which iconic children's toy?
quiz.explanation: While working on a heat pump experiment in his bathroom, Johnson accidentally shot a powerful stream of water and got the idea for the Super Soaker.

quiz.q: Before inventing the Super Soaker, Lonnie Johnson worked as an engineer for which organization?
choices: The U.S. Air Force and NASA
quiz.explanation: Johnson worked as a nuclear engineer for the U.S. Air Force and later as a systems engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

quiz.q: The Super Soaker became one of what?
choices: The best-selling toys of all time
The most recalled toys in history
The only water toys licensed by NASA
quiz.explanation: Since its release in 1990, the Super Soaker has generated over $1 billion in sales, making it one of the best-selling toys ever.

quiz.q: Beyond the Super Soaker, Johnson has continued research in what important technology field?
choices: Advanced energy storage and battery technology
quiz.explanation: Johnson founded Johnson Research and Development and has pursued breakthrough research in solid-state battery technology and energy storage.

quiz.q: As a child, Lonnie Johnson built a homemade what, demonstrating his early engineering genius?
quiz.explanation: As a teenager, Johnson built a homemade rocket fueled by jet fuel, which won him a science fair competition.

items.title: Louis Armstrong
items.description: Trumpeter, vocalist, and bandleader from New Orleans who is widely considered the most important figure in jazz history and one of the most influential musicians America has ever produced.

quiz.q: Louis Armstrong is most associated with playing which instrument?
quiz.explanation: Armstrong began on cornet and became the definitive jazz trumpet virtuoso, revolutionizing both instruments.

quiz.q: What nickname was Louis Armstrong given that became almost as famous as his name?
quiz.explanation: Armstrong had several nicknames: 'Satchmo' (short for 'Satchelmouth'), 'Pops,' and the early 'Dippermouth' — all became part of his legend.

quiz.q: Louis Armstrong grew up in which city, widely considered the birthplace of jazz?
quiz.explanation: Armstrong was born and raised in New Orleans, Louisiana, the city that gave birth to jazz.

quiz.q: Armstrong pioneered which vocal technique that became a signature element of jazz singing?
quiz.explanation: Armstrong helped popularize scat singing — improvising wordless vocalizations — which became a cornerstone of jazz vocal performance.

quiz.q: Which Louis Armstrong song became one of the best-selling singles in history?
choices: When the Saints Go Marching In
quiz.explanation: 'What a Wonderful World' (1967) became one of the most beloved and best-selling recordings in music history.

items.title: Lyda D Newman
items.description: Inventor and activist who in 1898 patented an improved hairbrush design and was also a prominent suffragist fighting for women's voting rights in New York.

quiz.q: Lyda D. Newman is celebrated for patenting an improvement to which everyday item?
quiz.explanation: Newman patented an improved hairbrush in 1898 that featured a compartment for cleaning out hair and debris — a design still used today.

quiz.q: What was innovative about Newman's hairbrush design?
choices: It had a built-in cleaning compartment
It was made of metal instead of wood
quiz.explanation: Her design included an open-air chamber between the bristles that allowed hair and dust to be easily shaken or cleaned out.

quiz.q: Beyond inventing, Lyda D. Newman was also active in what political movement?
quiz.explanation: Newman was a prominent suffragist who organized and advocated for women's right to vote in New York.

quiz.q: In what year did Lyda D. Newman receive her patent?
quiz.explanation: Newman was granted U.S. Patent 614,335 for her improved hairbrush on November 15, 1898.

quiz.q: Newman's dual legacy as inventor and activist makes her a symbol of what?
choices: Black women's ingenuity and civic leadership
quiz.explanation: She is celebrated as an early example of Black women's contributions to both invention and the struggle for civil and political rights.

items.title: Madam C J Walker
items.description: Entrepreneur and philanthropist who became one of the first American women to become a self-made millionaire by building a hair care empire catering to Black women.

quiz.q: Madam C.J. Walker is celebrated as one of the first American women to achieve what?
quiz.explanation: Walker built a hair care products empire that made her one of the first American women — and the first Black American woman — to become a self-made millionaire.

quiz.q: Madam C.J. Walker's business was built around products designed for which customers?
quiz.explanation: Walker developed and sold hair care products specifically designed to address the needs of Black women's hair.

quiz.q: Walker was born Sarah Breedlove in what circumstances?
choices: To formerly enslaved parents in Louisiana
To a free Black family in the North
To an immigrant family in New York
To a wealthy Black family in Atlanta
quiz.explanation: She was born Sarah Breedlove in 1867 in Louisiana to parents who had recently been freed from slavery.

quiz.q: Madam C.J. Walker was also known for her generous support of what causes?
choices: Civil rights organizations and Black education
quiz.explanation: She donated generously to the NAACP, the YMCA, Black schools, and anti-lynching campaigns, using her wealth to advance her community.

quiz.q: Walker's business model was innovative because it employed and empowered thousands of what?
quiz.explanation: Her nationwide sales force of Black women agents gave thousands of women economic independence and entrepreneurial opportunity.

items.title: Mae Jemison
items.description: Physician and NASA astronaut who in 1992 became the first African American woman to travel in space, aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour.

quiz.q: Mae Jemison made history in 1992 by becoming the first what?
choices: African American woman to travel in space
Woman to command a space shuttle
quiz.explanation: Jemison flew aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour in September 1992, becoming the first African American woman in space.

quiz.q: Before becoming an astronaut, Mae Jemison earned a degree in which medical field?
quiz.explanation: Jemison earned her M.D. from Cornell Medical College and worked as a physician, including serving as a Peace Corps medical officer in West Africa.

quiz.q: Mae Jemison served in NASA's mission specialist role aboard which space shuttle?
quiz.explanation: She flew on the STS-47 mission aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour in September 1992.

quiz.q: Mae Jemison has cited which fictional character as an inspiration for her pursuit of space travel?
quiz.explanation: Jemison has credited Lt. Uhura, played by Nichelle Nichols in Star Trek, as an early inspiration — and she later appeared in a Star Trek: The Next Generation episode.

quiz.q: After NASA, Mae Jemison founded which organization to advance science and technology education?
quiz.explanation: She founded the Jemison Group, a technology consulting company, and later led the 100 Year Starship project to advance interstellar travel research.

items.title: Malcolm X
items.description: Minister, activist, and Black nationalist leader whose powerful advocacy for Black self-determination and human rights made him one of the most influential figures of the 20th century.

quiz.q: Malcolm X was born with what birth name?
quiz.explanation: He was born Malcolm Little in Omaha, Nebraska in 1925, later taking the surname 'X' to replace what he called his slave name.

quiz.q: Malcolm X was a prominent minister and spokesperson for which organization?
quiz.explanation: Malcolm X became the most visible national spokesperson for the Nation of Islam under leader Elijah Muhammad.

quiz.q: Malcolm X's philosophy emphasized what approach to achieving Black freedom, initially contrasting with Martin Luther King Jr.?
quiz.explanation: Malcolm X advocated for Black self-determination and the right of Black people to defend themselves, famously declaring freedom 'by any means necessary.'

quiz.q: After breaking with the Nation of Islam and making a pilgrimage to Mecca, Malcolm X's views shifted toward what?
quiz.explanation: His hajj to Mecca in 1964 profoundly changed him, and he began speaking of human rights for all people regardless of race.

quiz.q: Malcolm X's autobiography, co-written with Alex Haley, is considered what?
choices: One of the most important nonfiction books of the 20th century
quiz.explanation: The Autobiography of Malcolm X (1965) is considered one of the most important and influential books in American literature.

items.title: Marie Van Brittan Brown
items.description: Inventor who in 1966 created the first home security system with closed-circuit television monitoring, laying the foundation for modern home security technology.

quiz.q: Marie Van Brittan Brown is credited with inventing what technology that protects homes today?
choices: Home security system with CCTV monitoring
quiz.explanation: Brown invented the first home security system featuring a closed-circuit television camera, peepholes, and a two-way microphone in 1966.

quiz.q: What was Brown's motivation for creating a home security system?
choices: Slow police response times in her Queens, NY neighborhood
Her work as a nurse dealing with hospital security
A government contract to develop the technology
quiz.explanation: Living in a neighborhood with high crime and slow police response times, Brown designed the system so she could monitor and control who entered her home.

quiz.q: Brown's invention included the ability to do what remotely?
choices: Unlock the front door and communicate with visitors
quiz.explanation: Her system allowed her to view visitors via camera, speak with them through a microphone, and remotely unlock the door — revolutionary for its time.

quiz.q: In what year did Marie Van Brittan Brown receive her patent?
quiz.explanation: She was granted U.S. Patent 3,482,037 for her home security system in 1969, three years after applying.

quiz.q: Brown's invention is considered the forerunner of what modern technologies?
choices: Modern home security systems and video doorbells
quiz.explanation: Every modern home security camera, video doorbell, and remote monitoring system traces its conceptual roots to Brown's 1966 invention.

items.title: Mark Dean
items.description: Computer engineer and IBM Fellow who co-created the IBM personal computer and holds three of the original nine PC patents, helping to define the modern computing era.

quiz.q: Mark Dean is celebrated for his role in developing which technology that changed the world?
quiz.explanation: Dean co-created the IBM PC in 1981, which became the standard for personal computing worldwide.

quiz.q: Mark Dean holds how many of the original nine patents for the IBM PC?
quiz.explanation: Dean holds three of the nine original IBM PC patents, covering fundamental aspects of the machine's design.

quiz.q: Mark Dean also led the team that developed what milestone in computing?
quiz.explanation: Dean led the IBM team that developed the first one-gigahertz computer chip in 1999, a landmark achievement in computing speed.

quiz.q: Dean achieved which prestigious honor at IBM, held by fewer than 70 people worldwide?
quiz.explanation: Mark Dean was named an IBM Fellow, the company's highest technical honor, held by fewer than 70 engineers in IBM's history.

quiz.q: Mark Dean also developed the ISA bus, which allowed computers to do what for the first time?
choices: Connect to peripheral devices like printers and monitors
quiz.explanation: The Industry Standard Architecture (ISA) bus allowed peripheral devices like monitors, printers, and keyboards to communicate with the PC.

items.title: Martin Luther King Jr.
items.description: Baptist minister and civil rights leader who guided the nonviolent movement that dismantled legal segregation in America, winning the Nobel Peace Prize and becoming a global symbol of justice.

quiz.q: Martin Luther King Jr. led the civil rights movement using which strategy?
quiz.explanation: Inspired by Mahatma Gandhi, King led the movement through nonviolent direct action including marches, sit-ins, and boycotts.

quiz.q: King delivered his famous 'I Have a Dream' speech at which 1963 event?
choices: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
quiz.explanation: King delivered the speech to over 250,000 people at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963.

quiz.q: Martin Luther King Jr. was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in what year?
quiz.explanation: King received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964, becoming the youngest recipient at the time at age 35.

quiz.q: King led the Montgomery Bus Boycott, which lasted how long and ended segregation on city buses?
quiz.explanation: The Montgomery Bus Boycott lasted 381 days from December 1955 to December 1956, ending with a Supreme Court ruling that bus segregation was unconstitutional.

quiz.q: Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated on April 4, 1968, in which city?
quiz.explanation: King was assassinated on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee, where he had come to support striking sanitation workers.

items.title: Mary Mcleod Bethune
items.description: Educator, activist, and presidential advisor who founded Bethune-Cookman University and became one of the most powerful Black women in American political history.

quiz.q: Mary McLeod Bethune founded which historically Black university in Daytona Beach, Florida?
quiz.explanation: Bethune founded the Daytona Normal and Industrial Institute for Girls in 1904, which later merged to become Bethune-Cookman University.

quiz.q: Bethune founded the National Council of Negro Women to do what?
choices: Unite Black women's organizations for political advocacy
Register Black women voters in the South
quiz.explanation: She founded the National Council of Negro Women (NCNW) in 1935 to unite Black women's organizations and amplify their political voice.

quiz.q: Mary McLeod Bethune served as an advisor to which U.S. president?
quiz.explanation: Bethune was a close advisor to President Franklin D. Roosevelt and directed the Division of Negro Affairs in the National Youth Administration.

quiz.q: Bethune was the fifteenth of how many children, born to formerly enslaved parents?
quiz.explanation: She was the fifteenth of seventeen children born to formerly enslaved parents in Mayesville, South Carolina.

quiz.q: Bethune started her school with almost no money and a founding student enrollment of how many?
quiz.explanation: She opened her school in 1904 with just five students, $1.50, and faith — building it into a nationally recognized institution.

items.title: Maya Angelou
items.description: Poet, memoirist, and civil rights activist whose autobiography I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings and whose poem at President Clinton's inauguration made her one of the most celebrated voices in American literature.
keywords: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings

quiz.q: Maya Angelou's most celebrated autobiography is titled what?
choices: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
All God's Children Need Traveling Shoes
quiz.explanation: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings (1969) is one of the most widely read autobiographies ever written and a cornerstone of American literature.

quiz.q: Maya Angelou delivered a poem at which president's inauguration in 1993?
quiz.explanation: Angelou recited 'On the Pulse of Morning' at President Bill Clinton's inauguration in January 1993.

quiz.q: As a child, Angelou stopped speaking for nearly five years after a traumatic experience. What ultimately helped her find her voice again?
choices: Literature and the encouragement of a teacher
quiz.explanation: A teacher named Bertha Flowers introduced young Maya to great literature and encouraged her to read aloud, helping restore her voice.

quiz.q: Maya Angelou worked closely with which civil rights leader as his Northern coordinator?
quiz.explanation: Angelou served as the Northern Coordinator for the Southern Christian Leadership Conference at the request of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

quiz.q: President Obama awarded Maya Angelou which honor in 2011?
quiz.explanation: President Obama awarded Angelou the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2011, the nation's highest civilian honor.

items.title: Michael Jackson
items.description: The King of Pop whose revolutionary music, dance moves, and music videos transformed the entertainment industry and made him the best-selling music artist of all time.

quiz.q: Michael Jackson is known by which legendary title?
quiz.explanation: Michael Jackson earned the title 'King of Pop' for his unprecedented dominance of popular music globally.

quiz.q: Michael Jackson first rose to fame as part of which family group?
quiz.explanation: Jackson began his career as a child performer with his brothers in The Jackson 5, signed to Motown Records.

quiz.q: Which 1982 album by Michael Jackson became the best-selling album of all time?
quiz.explanation: Thriller (1982) has sold an estimated 66–70 million copies worldwide, making it the best-selling album in history.

quiz.q: Michael Jackson is credited with popularizing which iconic dance move?
quiz.explanation: Jackson introduced the moonwalk to a global audience during his performance of 'Billie Jean' on the Motown 25 television special in 1983.

quiz.q: Jackson's music videos broke racial barriers when which network began airing them prominently?
quiz.explanation: MTV's decision to air Jackson's videos — especially 'Billie Jean' and 'Beat It' — broke an unofficial color barrier at the network and changed music television forever.

items.title: Michael Jordan
items.description: Widely considered the greatest basketball player of all time, Jordan won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and transformed basketball into a global cultural phenomenon.

quiz.q: Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with which team?
quiz.explanation: Jordan won all six of his NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls in two three-peats: 1991–1993 and 1996–1998.

quiz.q: How many NBA Finals MVP awards did Michael Jordan win?
quiz.explanation: Jordan won the NBA Finals MVP award all six times he appeared in the Finals — a perfect record.

quiz.q: Michael Jordan's Nike shoe line is known by what name?
quiz.explanation: The Air Jordan brand, launched in 1984, became one of the most successful and iconic sneaker lines in history.

quiz.q: Jordan famously hit a game-winning shot in the 1982 NCAA Championship game while playing for which university?
quiz.explanation: As a freshman at UNC, Jordan hit the game-winning shot against Georgetown to win the 1982 NCAA Championship.

quiz.q: The 2020 Netflix documentary series about Jordan and the Bulls' 1997-98 season was called what?
quiz.explanation: The Last Dance (2020) was a critically acclaimed documentary series chronicling Jordan's career and the Bulls' final championship run.

items.title: Michael Wilbon
items.description: Award-winning sports journalist and television personality best known as co-host of ESPN's Pardon the Interruption, one of the most successful sports debate shows in television history.

quiz.q: Michael Wilbon is best known as the co-host of which ESPN program?
quiz.explanation: Wilbon co-hosts Pardon the Interruption (PTI) with Tony Kornheiser, one of ESPN's most beloved and long-running shows.

quiz.q: Before television, Wilbon built his reputation as a sports columnist for which major newspaper?
quiz.explanation: Wilbon spent over 25 years as a sports columnist and reporter at The Washington Post before transitioning to television.

quiz.q: Wilbon grew up in which city, which shaped his passion for sports and journalism?
quiz.explanation: Wilbon grew up on the South Side of Chicago, where his love of sports — especially basketball — was formed.

quiz.q: Pardon the Interruption is known for what distinctive format?
choices: A fast-paced debate between two hosts with a countdown clock
quiz.explanation: PTI's signature format features Wilbon and Kornheiser debating sports topics with a visible countdown clock limiting each segment.

quiz.q: Wilbon is widely respected for combining sports commentary with what broader perspective?
choices: Race, culture, and social issues in sports
quiz.explanation: Wilbon is known for thoughtfully addressing the intersection of race, culture, and social justice within the world of sports.

items.title: Miles Davis
items.description: Trumpet virtuoso and bandleader who reinvented jazz multiple times, from bebop to cool jazz to fusion, making him one of the most innovative and influential musicians in history.

quiz.q: Miles Davis is celebrated as a master of which instrument?
quiz.explanation: Davis was one of the greatest trumpet players in history, known for his distinctive muted tone and lyrical phrasing.

quiz.q: Miles Davis's 1959 album is considered the best-selling jazz album of all time. What is it called?
quiz.explanation: Kind of Blue (1959) is the best-selling jazz album ever recorded and is widely considered one of the greatest albums in any genre.

quiz.q: Davis pioneered which jazz style in the late 1940s with his famous Birth of the Cool sessions?
quiz.explanation: The Birth of the Cool sessions (1949–1950) launched the cool jazz movement, a softer, more relaxed alternative to bebop.

quiz.q: Davis's 1970 album Bitches Brew revolutionized music by fusing jazz with what other genre?
quiz.explanation: Bitches Brew created jazz fusion by incorporating electric instruments and rock rhythms into jazz, changing both genres permanently.

quiz.q: Miles Davis was known for discovering and nurturing which other jazz legends in his bands?
choices: John Coltrane, Bill Evans, and Herbie Hancock
quiz.explanation: Davis's bands were famous incubators of talent — John Coltrane, Bill Evans, Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter, and many others launched their careers playing for him.

items.title: Misty Copeland
items.description: Ballet dancer who in 2015 became the first African American woman to be named principal dancer at American Ballet Theatre, one of the most prestigious ballet companies in the world.

quiz.q: Misty Copeland made history in 2015 by becoming the first Black woman to hold what position?
choices: Principal dancer at American Ballet Theatre
Director of a major ballet company
Lead in Swan Lake on Broadway
quiz.explanation: Copeland became the first African American woman named principal dancer at American Ballet Theatre (ABT) in its 75-year history.

quiz.q: Misty Copeland began studying ballet at what unusually late age for a professional dancer?
quiz.explanation: Most professional ballet dancers begin training around age 3–5, making Copeland's start at 13 remarkably late — and her rise to the top all the more extraordinary.

quiz.q: Copeland has been outspoken about the lack of what within classical ballet?
quiz.explanation: She has been a powerful advocate for racial diversity and inclusion in the overwhelmingly white world of classical ballet.

quiz.q: Misty Copeland starred in a production of which classic ballet that became a landmark moment for representation?
quiz.explanation: Her lead role in Swan Lake was a watershed moment, as Black ballerinas had rarely been cast in such iconic lead roles at major companies.

quiz.q: Beyond ballet, Copeland has expanded her reach through partnerships with which major brand?
quiz.explanation: Her Under Armour campaign featuring the poem 'I Will What I Want' became a viral sensation, bringing her story to millions beyond the ballet world.

items.title: Moms Mabley
items.description: Stand-up comedian and actress who pioneered the concept of the stand-up comedy persona and was one of the first women and first Black performers to headline at major venues.

quiz.q: Moms Mabley is recognized as a pioneer in which form of entertainment?
quiz.explanation: Mabley was one of the first stand-up comedians to develop a fully realized stage persona, predating most of what we think of as stand-up comedy.

quiz.q: Moms Mabley performed regularly on which famous entertainment circuit for Black artists during segregation?
quiz.explanation: She was a star on the Chitlin Circuit — the network of venues that welcomed Black performers during the era of segregation.

quiz.q: Moms Mabley was known for portraying what type of character in her comedy?
quiz.explanation: Her stage persona was a toothless, frumpy but sharp-witted old woman who dispensed wisdom and pointed social commentary.

quiz.q: Mabley was one of the first Black female performers to headline at which legendary New York venue?
quiz.explanation: She became a headliner at the Apollo Theater in Harlem, performing there for decades and becoming one of its most beloved acts.

quiz.q: Moms Mabley's comedy often included sharp commentary on what social topics?
quiz.explanation: Her humor cleverly addressed racism, the treatment of women, and the absurdity of social inequality — all wrapped in her beloved comic persona.

items.title: Monique
items.description: Comedian and actress from Baltimore who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her devastating performance in Precious and is celebrated for her fearless stand-up comedy.

quiz.q: Mo'Nique won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for which 2009 film?
quiz.explanation: Her portrayal of the monstrous yet complex Mary in Precious (2009) earned her the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress.

quiz.q: Before her Oscar win, Mo'Nique was primarily known for what type of performance?
quiz.explanation: Mo'Nique built her reputation as a fearless stand-up comedian known for her bold, unapologetic style.

quiz.q: Mo'Nique starred in which BET sitcom that ran from 2002 to 2008?
quiz.explanation: She starred as Nikki Parker in The Parkers, a spin-off of Moesha that became one of BET's most popular sitcoms.

quiz.q: Mo'Nique grew up in which city, which features prominently in her comedy and storytelling?
quiz.explanation: Mo'Nique grew up in Baltimore, Maryland, and her upbringing and roots there are central themes in her comedy.

quiz.q: Mo'Nique has been outspoken about what issue within the Hollywood industry?
choices: Racial and gender bias in pay and opportunity
quiz.explanation: She has been a vocal and public advocate against racial and gender bias in Hollywood compensation and opportunity.

items.title: Muhammed Ali
items.description: Three-time heavyweight boxing champion and global humanitarian who declared himself 'The Greatest' — and proved it both in the ring and in his courageous stands for justice outside it.

quiz.q: Muhammad Ali famously proclaimed himself to be what?
quiz.explanation: Ali's declaration 'I am the greatest!' became one of the most famous phrases in sports history — and his record largely backed it up.

quiz.q: Ali was stripped of his heavyweight title and banned from boxing for three years for what reason?
choices: Refusing military draft induction on religious grounds
Testing positive for a banned substance
quiz.explanation: Ali refused induction into the U.S. Army in 1967, citing his Muslim faith and opposition to the Vietnam War, and was banned from boxing as a result.

quiz.q: Ali was born with what name before converting to Islam?
quiz.explanation: He was born Cassius Marcellus Clay Jr. in Louisville, Kentucky, and changed his name after joining the Nation of Islam in 1964.

quiz.q: The legendary 1974 fight in which Ali defeated George Foreman in Zaire was nicknamed what?
quiz.explanation: The Rumble in the Jungle in Kinshasa, Zaire (now DRC) saw Ali use his famous 'rope-a-dope' strategy to knock out the heavily favored Foreman.

quiz.q: Muhammad Ali lit the Olympic cauldron at which Summer Olympic Games?
quiz.explanation: Ali lit the Olympic cauldron at the 1996 Atlanta Games in a moment that moved the world — his hands trembling from Parkinson's disease but his spirit unbroken.

items.title: Nas
items.description: Rapper from Queensbridge, New York whose debut album Illmatic is widely considered the greatest hip-hop album ever made, and whose career spans three decades of influential music.

quiz.q: Nas grew up in which New York City housing project that deeply influenced his music?
quiz.explanation: Nas grew up in the Queensbridge Houses in Queens, New York — the largest public housing development in North America — which is the backdrop for much of his music.

quiz.q: Nas's 1994 debut album is widely regarded as what?
choices: One of the greatest hip-hop albums ever made
The first concept album in hip-hop
quiz.explanation: Illmatic (1994) is consistently ranked as one of the greatest hip-hop albums ever recorded, lauded for its cinematic storytelling and lyrical density.

quiz.q: What is the title of Nas's celebrated 1994 debut album?
quiz.explanation: Illmatic (1994) announced Nas as a once-in-a-generation lyricist and is considered a foundational text of East Coast hip-hop.

quiz.q: Nas had a famous hip-hop feud in the early 2000s with which other rapper?
quiz.explanation: His feud with Jay-Z — including the diss track 'Ether' — is considered one of the greatest rap battles in hip-hop history.

quiz.q: Beyond music, Nas co-founded which venture capital firm investing in technology startups?
quiz.explanation: Nas co-founded QueensBridge Venture Partners, which has made early investments in companies including Dropbox, Lyft, and Ring.

items.title: Nicholas Brothers
items.description: Fayard and Harold Nicholas were a tap dancing duo whose acrobatic, gravity-defying performances in Hollywood films of the 1930s and 40s are considered the greatest tap dancing ever filmed.

quiz.q: The Nicholas Brothers — Fayard and Harold — were celebrated for mastering which art form?
quiz.explanation: The Nicholas Brothers were tap dancing virtuosos whose acrobatic style pushed the art form to levels never seen before or since.

quiz.q: The Nicholas Brothers' most celebrated film routine appeared in which 1943 movie?
quiz.explanation: Their routine in Stormy Weather (1943), which included splits down a flight of stairs, is considered the greatest tap dancing sequence ever filmed.

quiz.q: Fred Astaire called the Nicholas Brothers' Stormy Weather routine what?
choices: The greatest dance number ever put on film
The best tap routine he had ever seen
quiz.explanation: Fred Astaire reportedly called their Stormy Weather performance 'the greatest dance number ever put on film.'

quiz.q: Despite their Hollywood fame, the Nicholas Brothers faced what injustice?
choices: Racial segregation — they could not eat or stay with white co-stars
Having their pay withheld by studios
Being banned from performing in New York
quiz.explanation: Despite starring in Hollywood films, they were subject to Jim Crow segregation — unable to dine or stay in the same hotels as their white co-stars.

quiz.q: The Nicholas Brothers began performing as children at which legendary Harlem venue?
quiz.explanation: They began performing at the Cotton Club as children in the 1930s, sharing the stage with Duke Ellington and Cab Calloway.

items.title: Nina Simone
items.description: Singer, pianist, and civil rights activist whose unique blend of jazz, blues, classical, and soul — and her fierce protest music — made her one of the most powerful and uncompromising artists of the 20th century.

quiz.q: Nina Simone was celebrated for her mastery of which instrument in addition to her singing?
quiz.explanation: Simone was a classically trained pianist of exceptional ability, and her piano playing was as celebrated as her extraordinary voice.

quiz.q: Nina Simone wrote and performed which famous civil rights protest song after the 1963 Birmingham church bombing?
choices: To Be Young, Gifted and Black
quiz.explanation: 'Mississippi Goddam' (1964) was an angry, defiant response to the murder of Medgar Evers and the bombing of the 16th Street Baptist Church.

quiz.q: As a child prodigy, Nina Simone was denied admission to which prestigious music school, a rejection she attributed to racism?
quiz.explanation: She applied to the Curtis Institute of Music in Philadelphia and was rejected — she believed because she was Black, a wound that shaped her life and activism.

quiz.q: Nina Simone's style defied categorization, blending which genres?
choices: Jazz, blues, classical, folk, and gospel
quiz.explanation: Simone blended jazz, blues, classical, folk, gospel, and soul in a completely unique style that resisted any single label.

quiz.q: Nina Simone wrote 'To Be Young, Gifted and Black' as a tribute to which playwright and friend?
quiz.explanation: Simone wrote the song as a tribute to her close friend Lorraine Hansberry, the playwright who wrote A Raisin in the Sun.

items.title: Otis Boykin
items.description: Inventor who held 26 patents and created an improved electrical resistor used in computers, radios, and televisions, and most importantly in the pacemaker that has saved millions of lives.

quiz.q: Otis Boykin's most life-saving invention was a component used in which medical device?
quiz.explanation: Boykin invented an improved electrical resistor that became a critical component in cardiac pacemakers, helping to regulate heartbeats and save millions of lives.

quiz.q: How many patents did Otis Boykin hold during his career?
quiz.explanation: Boykin held 26 patents over his career, covering a wide range of electrical components and devices.

quiz.q: Boykin's improved resistor was also used in which common consumer electronics?
quiz.explanation: His precision resistors were used in computers, radios, televisions, and guided missiles, in addition to pacemakers.

quiz.q: Otis Boykin grew up in which Southern city before moving North for his career?
quiz.explanation: Boykin was born and raised in Dallas, Texas, and later moved to Chicago and then to Europe to advance his career.

quiz.q: What irony surrounds Otis Boykin's death in 1982?
choices: He died of heart failure — the condition his pacemaker component helped treat
He died before receiving credit for his inventions
He was never awarded a patent for his most important invention
He lived in poverty despite his life-saving work
quiz.explanation: Boykin died of heart failure in 1982 — a poignant irony given that his most celebrated invention helps regulate the very condition that killed him.

items.title: Patricia Bath
items.description: Ophthalmologist and inventor who became the first African American female doctor to receive a medical patent, for her Laserphaco Probe that restored sight to people who had been blind for decades.

quiz.q: Patricia Bath was the first African American woman doctor to receive a medical patent for what invention?
choices: The Laserphaco Probe for cataract surgery
A new type of contact lens
quiz.explanation: Bath invented the Laserphaco Probe in 1986, a laser device for precisely removing cataracts that restored sight to people who had been blind for over 30 years.

quiz.q: Patricia Bath specialized in which branch of medicine?
quiz.explanation: Bath was an ophthalmologist — a physician specializing in eye health and surgery — who dedicated her career to preventing and treating blindness.

quiz.q: Bath was also a co-founder of which organization dedicated to blindness prevention?
choices: American Institute for the Prevention of Blindness
quiz.explanation: She co-founded the American Institute for the Prevention of Blindness, which established that eyesight is a human right.

quiz.q: Bath was the first woman to hold what position at UCLA's Jules Stein Eye Institute?
choices: Faculty member in the ophthalmology residency program
quiz.explanation: Bath became the first woman faculty member in the ophthalmology residency program at UCLA's Jules Stein Eye Institute.

quiz.q: What was remarkable about Bath's determination to patent her Laserphaco Probe invention?
choices: She had to travel to Europe to find labs willing to develop it
She funded the research entirely herself
She invented it while raising five children alone
She completed the work after being told it was impossible
quiz.explanation: Unable to find U.S. labs willing to develop her laser technology, Bath traveled to Europe to complete her research and ultimately received patents in the U.S., Japan, Canada, and Europe.

items.title: Phillis Wheatly
items.description: The first African American and first enslaved person to publish a book of poetry in America, whose 1773 collection earned international acclaim and became a landmark of American literary history.

quiz.q: Phillis Wheatley holds which historic distinction in American literature?
choices: First African American to publish a book of poetry
First woman to win a poetry prize
First woman published by a Boston press
quiz.explanation: Wheatley was the first African American and the first enslaved person to publish a book of poetry in America, in 1773.

quiz.q: Wheatley was enslaved and brought to Boston from which continent as a child?
quiz.explanation: She was kidnapped from West Africa — likely Senegal or Gambia — and brought to Boston on a slave ship around 1761 at approximately age seven.

quiz.q: What was the title of Phillis Wheatley's 1773 published poetry collection?
choices: Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral
quiz.explanation: Her collection Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral was published in London in 1773 and received international praise.

quiz.q: Because publishers doubted an enslaved person could write poetry, Wheatley was required to do what before publication?
choices: Prove her authorship before a panel of Boston's leading men
Obtain a letter from her enslaver
quiz.explanation: She was examined by a panel of 18 prominent Boston men — including John Hancock — who questioned her to verify she had written her own poems.

quiz.q: George Washington personally invited Phillis Wheatley to do what after she wrote a poem in his honor?
choices: Publish her poem in a national gazette
Teach at a new school for freed Black people
Travel to England on his behalf
quiz.explanation: After Wheatley sent Washington a poem praising his leadership, he wrote back thanking her and invited her to visit his Cambridge, Massachusetts headquarters.

items.title: Phylicia Rashad
items.description: Actress, director, and educator best known for playing Clair Huxtable on The Cosby Show, who became the first Black woman to win the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play.

quiz.q: Phylicia Rashad is best known for playing which iconic television character?
choices: Clair Huxtable on The Cosby Show
Claire Kyle on My Wife and Kids
quiz.explanation: Rashad's portrayal of attorney and mother Clair Huxtable on The Cosby Show (1984–1992) made her one of the most beloved figures in television history.

quiz.q: Phylicia Rashad made history on Broadway by becoming the first Black woman to win what award?
choices: Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play
Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Actress
quiz.explanation: She won the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play in 2004 for her role in A Raisin in the Sun, becoming the first Black woman to win in that category.

quiz.q: Rashad won her Tony for a revival of which classic American play?
quiz.explanation: She starred in the 2004 Broadway revival of Lorraine Hansberry's A Raisin in the Sun, earning her historic Tony Award.

quiz.q: Beyond acting, Phylicia Rashad has served in what educational role?
choices: Dean of the College of Fine Arts at Howard University
Director of Drama at Spelman College
Artistic Director of the Apollo Theater
quiz.explanation: Rashad became the founding Dean of the College of Fine Arts at Howard University, her alma mater, in 2021.

quiz.q: Clair Huxtable was celebrated as a groundbreaking TV character because she portrayed Black women as what?
choices: Professional, educated, and fully realized human beings
quiz.explanation: Clair Huxtable — a Harvard-educated attorney and devoted mother — challenged and transformed the representation of Black women on American television.

items.title: Rihanna
items.description: Global music superstar, entrepreneur, and philanthropist from Barbados who became one of the best-selling music artists of all time and built the Fenty Beauty and Savage X Fenty empires.

quiz.q: Rihanna is from which Caribbean island nation?
quiz.explanation: Rihanna was born and raised in Bridgetown, Barbados, and is one of the most celebrated figures in her nation's history.

quiz.q: Rihanna founded which revolutionary beauty brand celebrated for its broad range of skin tones?
quiz.explanation: Fenty Beauty launched in 2017 with 40 foundation shades, disrupting the beauty industry by prioritizing inclusivity across all skin tones.

quiz.q: Rihanna became a billionaire primarily through which business venture rather than her music?
choices: Fenty Beauty and Savage X Fenty
quiz.explanation: Her Fenty Beauty and Savage X Fenty lingerie businesses made her a billionaire — with the majority of her wealth coming from business, not music.

quiz.q: Rihanna performed at which major American sporting event's halftime show in 2023?
quiz.explanation: Rihanna headlined the Apple Music Super Bowl LVII halftime show in February 2023 in Glendale, Arizona.

quiz.q: Barbados appointed Rihanna as what official title in 2021?
quiz.explanation: Upon becoming a republic, Barbados named Rihanna an Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary — its highest diplomatic designation.

items.title: Robyn Rihanna Fenty
items.description: The full birth name of the global icon known as Rihanna — Robyn Rihanna Fenty — whose identity as a Barbadian woman of African descent is central to her artistry and entrepreneurial mission.

quiz.q: Robyn Rihanna Fenty is better known to the world by which single name?
quiz.explanation: She performs and is known globally as Rihanna, her middle name, though her full birth name is Robyn Rihanna Fenty.

quiz.q: The Fenty name has become a global brand. What does Rihanna's Fenty Beauty brand stand for?
choices: Inclusive beauty for all skin tones
quiz.explanation: Fenty Beauty was founded on the principle of beauty for all, launching with an unprecedented 40 foundation shades to serve people of every skin tone.

quiz.q: Rihanna's Fenty name is tied to her heritage from which island?
quiz.explanation: The Fenty family name comes from her father's Barbadian heritage, and Rihanna has made her island identity central to her global brand.

quiz.q: Rihanna's fashion label Fenty was launched in partnership with which luxury fashion group?
quiz.explanation: Rihanna's Fenty fashion house was launched in partnership with LVMH (Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy), making her the first Black woman to lead an LVMH brand.

quiz.q: As Robyn Rihanna Fenty the philanthropist, she founded which charitable organization?
quiz.explanation: She founded the Clara Lionel Foundation in 2012, named after her grandparents, which funds education and emergency response programs globally.

items.title: Ronin Roberts
items.description: Young activist and community leader who has dedicated his life to uplifting youth in underserved communities through education, mentorship, and civic engagement.

quiz.q: Ronin Roberts is celebrated primarily for his work in what area?
quiz.explanation: Ronin Roberts is known for his dedication to uplifting young people in underserved communities through activism and mentorship.

quiz.q: What is a central focus of Ronin Roberts's community work?
choices: Empowering youth through education and mentorship
quiz.explanation: Roberts focuses on connecting young people with educational resources, mentors, and civic opportunities to help them reach their potential.

quiz.q: Roberts represents a generation of young Black leaders who are working to create change through what means?
quiz.explanation: Like many young community leaders, Roberts channels his energy into grassroots work that directly impacts the lives of young people in his community.

quiz.q: What quality is Ronin Roberts most recognized for within his community?
choices: Inspiring young people to believe in their own potential
quiz.explanation: Roberts is known for his ability to inspire young people and help them see their own worth and potential for positive impact.

quiz.q: Ronin Roberts's inclusion on this list reflects what broader truth about Black history?
choices: It is being made every day by people of all ages
Change only comes from famous people
Youth have no role in social progress
quiz.explanation: His presence reminds us that Black history is not just the past — it is being made right now by young people committed to justice and community.

items.title: Scott Joplin
items.description: Composer and pianist known as the King of Ragtime, whose infectious syncopated compositions like 'Maple Leaf Rag' defined an era and laid the rhythmic foundation for jazz and popular American music.

quiz.q: Scott Joplin is known by which royal title in American music history?
quiz.explanation: Joplin earned the title 'King of Ragtime' for his mastery and prolific output of ragtime compositions.

quiz.q: What is the title of Scott Joplin's most famous composition, published in 1899?
quiz.explanation: 'Maple Leaf Rag' (1899) was the first sheet music to sell one million copies and made Joplin the most celebrated composer in America.

quiz.q: Scott Joplin's music was featured in which 1973 Academy Award-winning film, introducing him to a new generation?
quiz.explanation: The Sting (1973), starring Paul Newman and Robert Redford, featured Joplin's music throughout and won the Oscar for Best Original Score.

quiz.q: Joplin spent years composing which grand opera that he considered his masterwork?
quiz.explanation: Treemonisha was a full-length opera Joplin composed and promoted for years, though it was not professionally staged until 1972 — 55 years after his death.

quiz.q: Scott Joplin was posthumously awarded which prestigious honor in 1976?
quiz.explanation: Joplin was posthumously awarded a Special Pulitzer Prize in 1976 for his contributions to American music.

items.title: Serena Williams
items.description: Tennis legend who won 23 Grand Slam singles titles — the most by any player in the Open Era — and transformed women's tennis with her athleticism, power, and iconic presence.

quiz.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Serena Williams win during her career?
quiz.explanation: Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, the most by any player in the Open Era of professional tennis.

quiz.q: Serena Williams won the 2017 Australian Open while how far along in her pregnancy?
quiz.explanation: Williams won the 2017 Australian Open while approximately eight weeks pregnant, making it arguably the greatest Grand Slam victory ever.

quiz.q: Serena Williams won her first Grand Slam title at which tournament in 1999?
quiz.explanation: Williams won her first Grand Slam title at the 1999 US Open at just 17 years old.

quiz.q: Along with her sister Venus, Serena has won how many Olympic gold medals in doubles?
quiz.explanation: Serena and Venus won Olympic gold in doubles together in 2000, 2008, and 2012 — three gold medals as a team.

quiz.q: After retiring from tennis, Serena Williams announced she was pursuing which new venture?
choices: Venture capital investing through Serena Ventures
quiz.explanation: Williams founded Serena Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on investing in companies led by diverse founders.

items.title: Shawn Carter
items.description: Known as JAY-Z, Shawn Carter rose from the Marcy Projects in Brooklyn to become one of the greatest rappers of all time and one of hip-hop's first billionaires through music and business.

quiz.q: Shawn Carter is known worldwide by which rap name?
quiz.explanation: He is known as JAY-Z, one of the most celebrated and commercially successful rappers in history.

quiz.q: JAY-Z grew up in which New York City housing project that shaped his worldview and lyrics?
quiz.explanation: Carter grew up in the Marcy Houses public housing project in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York.

quiz.q: JAY-Z co-founded which record label that launched careers including Kanye West and Rihanna?
quiz.explanation: He co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records in 1995, which became one of hip-hop's most influential labels before he later founded Roc Nation.

quiz.q: JAY-Z became hip-hop's first billionaire through music and which diverse business ventures?
choices: Music streaming, sports management, liquor brands, and real estate
quiz.explanation: His wealth comes from a diverse portfolio including the Tidal streaming service, Armand de Brignac champagne, D'Ussé cognac, Roc Nation sports management, and real estate.

quiz.q: JAY-Z holds the record for the most Grammy nominations by which artist type?
choices: Any solo artist in Grammy history
Any rapper born in New York
quiz.explanation: JAY-Z holds the record for the most Grammy nominations by any solo artist in Grammy history.

items.title: Sheryl Underwood
items.description: Stand-up comedian, actress, and television co-host of The Talk who rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most recognizable faces in daytime television.

quiz.q: Sheryl Underwood is best known as a co-host of which daytime television program?
quiz.explanation: Underwood has been a co-host of CBS's The Talk since 2011, becoming one of its most popular and long-running panelists.

quiz.q: Before television, Sheryl Underwood built her reputation through what career?
quiz.explanation: Underwood was a stand-up comedian for many years, performing at major venues and comedy festivals across the country.

quiz.q: Sheryl Underwood made history as the first woman elected to lead which organization?
choices: Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity's National Board
quiz.explanation: Underwood became the first woman elected to the national board of Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity, Inc., a historically Black Greek organization.

quiz.q: Underwood grew up in difficult circumstances including what challenging situation?
choices: Growing up in the foster care system
quiz.explanation: Underwood has spoken openly about experiencing homelessness as a child, and her journey from poverty to television stardom is a central part of her story.

quiz.q: On The Talk, Sheryl Underwood is known for bringing what quality to the program?
choices: Bold humor and honest conversation about race and culture
quiz.explanation: Underwood is celebrated for her fearless humor and her willingness to have honest, sometimes uncomfortable conversations about race, identity, and culture.

items.title: Shirley Chisholm
items.description: Educator and politician who in 1968 became the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Congress, and in 1972 became the first Black candidate and first woman to seek the Democratic presidential nomination.

quiz.q: Shirley Chisholm made history in 1968 by becoming the first what?
choices: Black woman elected to the U.S. Congress
Black woman to run for president
Woman to serve on the House Education Committee
Black woman elected to the Senate
quiz.explanation: Chisholm was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives from New York in 1968, becoming the first Black woman in Congress.

quiz.q: Shirley Chisholm ran for President in 1972 representing which party?
quiz.explanation: Chisholm sought the Democratic Party presidential nomination in 1972, becoming the first Black candidate and first woman to seek a major party's presidential nomination.

quiz.q: What was Shirley Chisholm's famous campaign slogan?
quiz.explanation: 'Unbossed and Unbought' was her motto — reflecting her fierce independence from political machines and special interests.

quiz.q: Before her congressional career, Chisholm worked in which field?
quiz.explanation: Chisholm was an educator and administrator in early childhood education and worked in child welfare before entering politics.

quiz.q: Shirley Chisholm was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom posthumously by which president?
quiz.explanation: President Barack Obama awarded Chisholm the Presidential Medal of Freedom posthumously in 2015.

items.title: Sidney Poitier
items.description: Actor and diplomat who in 1964 became the first Black man to win the Academy Award for Best Actor, and whose dignified, powerful performances changed how Black people were represented in Hollywood.

quiz.q: Sidney Poitier made history in 1964 by becoming the first Black man to win what?
quiz.explanation: Poitier won the Academy Award for Best Actor for Lilies of the Field (1963), the first Black man to win in that category.

quiz.q: Sidney Poitier won his Oscar for which film?
choices: In the Heat of the Night
quiz.explanation: His warm, dignified performance as Homer Smith in Lilies of the Field (1963) earned him the historic Oscar.

quiz.q: Poitier was known for carefully selecting roles that portrayed Black men with what quality?
quiz.explanation: Poitier was deliberate about choosing roles that showed Black men as dignified, complex human beings at a time when Hollywood rarely offered such portrayals.

quiz.q: After his acting career, Sidney Poitier served as what for the Bahamas?
quiz.explanation: Poitier, who was born in the Bahamas, served as the Bahamian Ambassador to Japan from 1997 to 2007.

quiz.q: Three of Poitier's most celebrated 1967 films all dealt with what theme?
choices: Racial prejudice and integration in America
quiz.explanation: In the Heat of the Night, Guess Who's Coming to Dinner, and To Sir, with Love (all 1967) each confronted racial prejudice and the possibility of a more integrated America.

items.title: Simone Biles
items.description: The most decorated gymnast in history whose gravity-defying skills, multiple world and Olympic titles, and courageous advocacy for mental health made her a generational icon.

quiz.q: Simone Biles is considered the greatest of all time in which sport?
quiz.explanation: Biles is the most decorated gymnast in history, with more World Championship and Olympic medals than any other gymnast.

quiz.q: Simone Biles has had multiple gymnastics skills named after her. What does that mean?
choices: She was the first to perform and compete them at a World Championship or Olympics
She invented them in training only
She performed them more times than anyone else
She was awarded the naming rights by the IOC
quiz.explanation: Under gymnastics rules, skills are named after the first person to perform them in international competition — Biles has had five skills named after her.

quiz.q: At the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, Biles made headlines for withdrawing from several events to prioritize what?
choices: A physical injury to her ankle
A protest against the judging panel
quiz.explanation: Biles withdrew from several events at the Tokyo Games citing her mental health, sparking a global conversation about athlete wellbeing.

quiz.q: Simone Biles returned to elite competition in 2023-24 and won gold at which games?
choices: She did not compete again after Tokyo
quiz.explanation: Biles made a triumphant return, winning multiple medals including gold at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

quiz.q: Biles has been outspoken about being a survivor of abuse by which disgraced doctor?
quiz.explanation: Biles was one of the many athletes who spoke out about being abused by USA Gymnastics team doctor Larry Nassar, helping bring him to justice.

items.title: Somore
items.description: Stand-up comedian celebrated for her bold, unapologetic humor that centers the experiences of Black women, making her one of the most distinctive voices in comedy.

quiz.q: Somore is best known as what type of entertainer?
quiz.explanation: Somore is a celebrated stand-up comedian known for her fearless, witty, and unapologetic comedy.

quiz.q: Somore's comedy is especially known for speaking to the experiences of which audience?
quiz.explanation: Somore's comedy centers the lives, relationships, and perspectives of Black women with humor and honesty.

quiz.q: Somore gained wider recognition through appearances on which influential comedy platform?
quiz.explanation: Somore gained national recognition through her appearances on Def Comedy Jam, one of the most important platforms in Black stand-up comedy.

quiz.q: What distinguishes Somore's comedic style?
choices: Bold, unfiltered honesty about relationships and womanhood
quiz.explanation: Somore is known for her bold, confident, and unapologetically honest comedy about relationships, womanhood, and Black life.

quiz.q: Somore represents a tradition of Black female comedians who paved the way for future performers. Who is one pioneer she follows?
quiz.explanation: Somore follows in the tradition of pioneering Black female comedians like Moms Mabley, who blazed the trail for women to command stages with bold, authentic humor.

items.title: Spike Lee
items.description: Filmmaker and cultural provocateur whose groundbreaking films like Do the Right Thing and Malcolm X gave voice to the Black American experience and challenged Hollywood to tell those stories.

quiz.q: Spike Lee is celebrated primarily as what type of artist?
quiz.explanation: Lee is one of the most important filmmakers in American history, known for films that boldly explore race, politics, and Black culture.

quiz.q: Which 1989 Spike Lee film about racial tensions in Brooklyn is considered one of the greatest films ever made?
quiz.explanation: Do the Right Thing (1989) is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most important American films ever made.

quiz.q: Spike Lee's three-and-a-half-hour 1992 biopic starred Denzel Washington as which leader?
quiz.explanation: Malcolm X (1992) starred Denzel Washington in a widely praised performance that Lee fought passionately to direct.

quiz.q: Spike Lee won his first competitive Academy Award for which 2018 film?
quiz.explanation: Lee won the Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay for BlacKkKlansman (2018), based on the true story of a Black detective who infiltrated the KKK.

quiz.q: Spike Lee is also known as a lifelong devoted fan of which NBA team?
quiz.explanation: Lee is one of the most famous New York Knicks fans in the world, often seen courtside at Madison Square Garden.

items.title: Stephen A Smith
items.description: Sports journalist, commentator, and media personality who became one of the highest-paid and most recognizable voices in sports media through his work on ESPN's First Take.

quiz.q: Stephen A. Smith is best known as the co-host of which ESPN debate program?
quiz.explanation: Smith is the centerpiece of ESPN's First Take, one of the most-watched sports debate shows on television.

quiz.q: Stephen A. Smith grew up in which New York City borough?
quiz.explanation: Smith grew up in the Hollis neighborhood of Queens, New York, and his upbringing there shaped his passion for sports and communication.

quiz.q: Before his television career, Smith worked as a sports reporter for which major newspaper?
quiz.explanation: Smith worked as a sports reporter and columnist at the Philadelphia Inquirer, where he built his reputation covering the NBA.

quiz.q: Smith's ESPN contract, reportedly worth over $12 million annually, made him what in sports media?
choices: The highest-paid sports media personality in history
The first Black anchor at ESPN
The most-followed sports personality on social media
quiz.explanation: Smith's multi-year contract reportedly worth over $12 million annually made him the highest-paid personality in sports media history.

quiz.q: Stephen A. Smith is known for his passionate commentary style characterized by what?
choices: Loud, confident opinions delivered with theatrical flair
quiz.explanation: Smith's bombastic, passionate delivery and unfiltered hot takes have made him one of the most entertaining and polarizing figures in sports media.

items.title: Thurgood Marshall
items.description: Civil rights attorney who successfully argued Brown v. Board of Education before the Supreme Court, ending legal school segregation, before becoming the first Black Justice on the Supreme Court.

quiz.q: Thurgood Marshall is celebrated for arguing which landmark Supreme Court case that ended school segregation?
quiz.explanation: Marshall argued and won Brown v. Board of Education in 1954, in which the Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional.

quiz.q: Thurgood Marshall made history in 1967 by becoming the first what?
choices: African American Justice on the U.S. Supreme Court
Black Solicitor General of the United States
Black attorney to argue before the Supreme Court
quiz.explanation: President Lyndon B. Johnson appointed Marshall as the first African American Associate Justice of the Supreme Court in 1967.

quiz.q: Marshall worked for years as the chief legal counsel for which civil rights organization?
quiz.explanation: Marshall served as the chief counsel for the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund, where he won 29 of the 32 cases he argued before the Supreme Court.

quiz.q: Before being nominated to the Supreme Court, Marshall served as the U.S. Solicitor General, meaning he did what?
choices: Argued the federal government's cases before the Supreme Court
Served as the Attorney General's deputy
quiz.explanation: As Solicitor General from 1965 to 1967, Marshall represented the United States government in cases before the Supreme Court.

quiz.q: Marshall was denied admission to the University of Maryland Law School because of his race. He later argued a case that desegregated that very school. What was that case?
choices: Missouri ex rel. Gaines v. Canada
quiz.explanation: In a personal triumph, Marshall argued Murray v. Pearson (1935), which desegregated the University of Maryland Law School that had rejected him.

items.title: Tupac Amaru Shakur
items.description: Rapper, poet, and actor whose unflinching music about Black poverty, police brutality, and resilience made him one of the best-selling and most influential artists in hip-hop history.

quiz.q: Tupac Shakur is considered one of the greatest and most influential artists in what genre?
quiz.explanation: Tupac is consistently ranked among the greatest rappers of all time and has sold over 75 million records worldwide.

quiz.q: Tupac's mother Afeni Shakur was a member of which political organization that influenced his worldview?
quiz.explanation: His mother Afeni Shakur was a Black Panther Party activist, and that political consciousness deeply shaped Tupac's music and beliefs.

quiz.q: Which of Tupac's albums, released while he was in prison, became one of the best-selling rap albums ever?
quiz.explanation: Me Against the World (1995) debuted at number one while Tupac was incarcerated, making him the first artist to have a number-one album while in prison.

quiz.q: Tupac also had a notable career as an actor. Which 1993 film showcased his dramatic acting ability?
quiz.explanation: Poetic Justice (1993), in which he co-starred with Janet Jackson, demonstrated his considerable acting talent alongside his music career.

quiz.q: Tupac Shakur was shot and killed in Las Vegas in September of which year?
quiz.explanation: Tupac was fatally shot in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996, and died six days later at age 25.

items.title: Tyler Perry
items.description: Playwright, filmmaker, and entrepreneur who built a media empire from homelessness, creating iconic characters like Madea and becoming the first Black person to own a major Hollywood studio.

quiz.q: Tyler Perry is best known for creating which beloved comedic character?
quiz.explanation: Madea — the tough, wise, gun-toting grandmother Perry plays himself — became one of the most popular characters in African American entertainment.

quiz.q: Tyler Perry made history by becoming the first Black person to own what?
quiz.explanation: Perry built Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta, Georgia, on the grounds of a former Confederate army base, becoming the first Black person to own a major Hollywood studio.

quiz.q: Before his success, Tyler Perry overcame what significant hardship?
quiz.explanation: Perry has spoken openly about being homeless and living out of his car at times while trying to get his first stage play produced.

quiz.q: Perry built his early empire through which format before transitioning to film and television?
choices: Stage plays touring the Chitlin Circuit
quiz.explanation: Perry built a devoted audience through stage plays touring the urban theater circuit before moving into film with the Madea franchise.

quiz.q: Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta sits on how many acres, making it one of the largest studio lots in the country?
quiz.explanation: Tyler Perry Studios sits on 330 acres in southwest Atlanta, making it one of the largest studio facilities in the United States.

items.title: Viola Davis
items.description: Emmy, Tony, and Oscar-winning actress who became the first Black woman to win the Triple Crown of Acting, celebrated for her raw, powerful performances and her advocacy for diverse storytelling.

quiz.q: Viola Davis made history as the first Black woman to achieve what acting milestone?
choices: Win the Triple Crown of Acting — Emmy, Tony, and Oscar
Win an Oscar for two different films
Win an Emmy for a dramatic and comedic role
quiz.explanation: Davis is the first Black woman — and one of only a handful of performers ever — to win the Emmy, Tony, and Oscar, known as the Triple Crown of Acting.

quiz.q: Viola Davis won her Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for which film?
choices: How to Get Away with Murder
quiz.explanation: Davis won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for Fences (2016), adapted from August Wilson's play and directed by Denzel Washington.

quiz.q: Davis won an Emmy for starring in which ABC legal drama?
choices: How to Get Away with Murder
quiz.explanation: She won the Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for How to Get Away with Murder, becoming the first Black woman to win in that category.

quiz.q: Davis grew up in extreme poverty in which state, an upbringing she has spoken about with powerful honesty?
quiz.explanation: Davis grew up in dire poverty in Central Falls, Rhode Island, and has spoken movingly about hunger, rodents, and the determination that drove her to Juilliard and stardom.

quiz.q: Viola Davis published a memoir in 2022 about her life and career. What was it called?
quiz.explanation: Her memoir Finding Me (2022) was a New York Times bestseller, telling the story of her extraordinary journey from poverty to the pinnacle of acting.

items.title: W.E.B. DuBois
items.description: Scholar, author, civil rights activist, and co-founder of the NAACP whose concept of 'double consciousness' and landmark work The Souls of Black Folk shaped American thought on race for generations.

quiz.q: W.E.B. Du Bois was the first African American to earn a PhD from which university?
quiz.explanation: Du Bois earned his doctorate from Harvard University in 1895, the first African American to do so.

quiz.q: Du Bois co-founded which major civil rights organization in 1909?
quiz.explanation: Du Bois was a co-founder of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in 1909.

quiz.q: What is the title of Du Bois's 1903 masterwork that introduced the concept of 'double consciousness'?
quiz.explanation: The Souls of Black Folk (1903) introduced the concept of 'double consciousness' — the sense of always looking at oneself through the eyes of a racist society.

quiz.q: Du Bois famously disagreed with Booker T. Washington over what central issue?
choices: Whether Black Americans should demand full civil rights or focus on vocational education
Whether Black Americans should emigrate to Africa
Whether to support World War I
quiz.explanation: Du Bois insisted on full civil and political rights for Black Americans, while Washington emphasized economic self-help and vocational training as a first step.

quiz.q: W.E.B. Du Bois lived to be 95 years old and spent his final years living in which African country?
quiz.explanation: Du Bois moved to Ghana in 1961 at the invitation of President Kwame Nkrumah, and died there in 1963, the day before the March on Washington.

items.title: Wallace Amos
items.description: Entrepreneur and literacy advocate known as Wally Amos who founded Famous Amos cookies, creating one of America's most beloved snack brands and later dedicating his life to promoting reading.

quiz.q: Wallace Amos is best known for founding which iconic American cookie brand?
quiz.explanation: Wally Amos founded Famous Amos chocolate chip cookies in 1975, opening the first store on Sunset Boulevard in Hollywood.

quiz.q: Before becoming a cookie entrepreneur, Wallace Amos worked in which industry?
quiz.explanation: Amos was a talent agent at William Morris Agency, where he became the first Black agent and represented artists like Simon & Garfunkel.

quiz.q: Famous Amos cookies were launched in 1975 with help from celebrity investors. Which musicians helped fund his first store?
quiz.explanation: Marvin Gaye and Helen Reddy were among the friends and celebrities who invested in or supported the launch of Famous Amos.

quiz.q: After Famous Amos, Wallace Amos dedicated much of his time to advocating for what cause?
quiz.explanation: Amos became a passionate literacy advocate, serving as a national spokesperson for Literacy Volunteers of America.

quiz.q: Wallace Amos's Famous Amos cookies were notable as one of the first what in American business?
quiz.explanation: Famous Amos was a pioneering gourmet specialty cookie brand and one of the first nationally recognized Black-owned food companies.

items.title: Wanda Sykes
items.description: Comedian, actress, and writer celebrated for her razor-sharp wit and her courage in being openly gay, making her one of the most distinctive and groundbreaking voices in American comedy.

quiz.q: Wanda Sykes is celebrated primarily as what type of entertainer?
quiz.explanation: Sykes is one of the sharpest stand-up comedians in America and a celebrated actress known for her fearless, witty performances.

quiz.q: Wanda Sykes made a courageous public announcement in 2008. What did she reveal?
choices: That she was running for public office
quiz.explanation: Sykes publicly came out as gay in 2008 at a marriage equality rally in Las Vegas, becoming one of the most prominent openly gay Black entertainers in America.

quiz.q: Sykes began her comedy career after leaving what previous profession?
quiz.explanation: Before comedy, Sykes worked as a procurement specialist for the National Security Agency (NSA) — a fact that surprises many fans.

quiz.q: Wanda Sykes played which recurring character on the hit series Curb Your Enthusiasm?
quiz.explanation: Sykes has appeared as a version of herself on Curb Your Enthusiasm, one of her many memorable TV appearances.

quiz.q: Sykes was the first openly gay Black woman and first Black female comedian to perform at which prestigious event?
quiz.explanation: Sykes performed at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in 2009, making history as the first openly gay Black woman and first Black female comedian to headline the event.

items.title: Whitney Houston
items.description: Vocalist widely considered the greatest singer of all time, whose extraordinary voice, record-breaking albums, and iconic performances made her one of the best-selling music artists in history.

quiz.q: Whitney Houston is widely considered by many to have what distinction as a vocalist?
choices: The greatest voice in popular music history
The best-selling artist of the 1980s only
quiz.explanation: Houston is widely considered to possess the greatest voice in popular music history, with a range, power, and emotional depth unmatched by any other singer.

quiz.q: Whitney Houston's recording of 'I Will Always Love You' for which 1992 film became one of the best-selling singles ever?
