quiz.explanation: Her version of 'I Will Always Love You' for The Bodyguard (1992) spent 14 weeks at number one and became one of the best-selling singles in history.

quiz.q: Whitney Houston's debut album in 1985 was notable for what record-breaking achievement?
choices: It produced more number-one singles than any debut album in history
It was the best-selling debut album of all time
It made her the youngest artist to top the charts
It debuted at number one in every country simultaneously
quiz.explanation: Her debut album produced seven consecutive number-one singles, a record that still stands today.

quiz.q: Before her recording career, Houston was raised in a deeply musical family. Her mother was which celebrated gospel and soul singer?
quiz.explanation: Her mother Cissy Houston was a celebrated gospel and soul singer, and her cousin was Dionne Warwick — music was in Whitney's blood from birth.

quiz.q: Whitney Houston's Super Bowl XXV performance of which song is considered the greatest national anthem performance ever?
quiz.explanation: Her 1991 Super Bowl XXV rendition of The Star-Spangled Banner is universally regarded as the greatest performance of the national anthem in history.

items.title: Whoopi Goldberg
items.description: Comedian, actress, and talk show host who is one of the rare EGOT winners — having won an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony — and one of the most recognized entertainers in the world.

quiz.q: Whoopi Goldberg is one of the few entertainers to have achieved what rare distinction?
choices: EGOT — winning an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony
A Pulitzer Prize and an Oscar
Awards in acting, directing, and writing
Wins at the Oscars across three different decades
quiz.explanation: Goldberg is one of only a handful of people to achieve EGOT status — winning Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Awards.

quiz.q: Whoopi Goldberg won her Academy Award for which film?
quiz.explanation: She won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for her role as Oda Mae Brown in Ghost (1990).

quiz.q: Goldberg received her first Oscar nomination for playing which character in The Color Purple?
quiz.explanation: Her debut film performance as Celie in The Color Purple (1985) earned her an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress.

quiz.q: Whoopi Goldberg has been a co-host of which long-running daytime talk show since 2007?
quiz.explanation: Goldberg has been a moderator and co-host of The View since 2007, becoming one of the show's most iconic panelists.

quiz.q: In the Star Trek franchise, Whoopi Goldberg played which beloved recurring character?
choices: Kai Opaka on Deep Space Nine
quiz.explanation: Goldberg played the wise and mysterious bartender Guinan on Star Trek: The Next Generation — a role she requested after being inspired by Nichelle Nichols's Lt. Uhura.

items.title: Will Smith
items.description: Rapper, actor, and producer who rose from Philadelphia to become one of the biggest box office stars in Hollywood history, achieving rare success across music, television, and film.

quiz.q: Will Smith first rose to national fame through which television series?
quiz.explanation: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air (1990–1996), in which Smith played a fictionalized version of himself, made him a household name.

quiz.q: Will Smith began his career as a rapper under what name?
quiz.explanation: Smith performed as The Fresh Prince alongside DJ Jazzy Jeff, winning the first-ever Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance in 1989.

quiz.q: Will Smith won his first Academy Award for Best Actor for playing which real-life tennis father?
quiz.explanation: Smith won the Oscar for Best Actor for his portrayal of Venus and Serena Williams's father Richard Williams in King Richard (2021).

quiz.q: Will Smith has starred in numerous blockbuster films. Which 1996 film made him one of Hollywood's biggest action stars?
quiz.explanation: Independence Day (1996) was the highest-grossing film of that year and established Smith as a major Hollywood action star.

quiz.q: Will Smith grew up in which Philadelphia neighborhood that he has often referenced in his work?
quiz.explanation: Smith grew up in West Philadelphia — a fact immortalized in The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air's famous theme song, which he largely wrote himself.

items.title: Wilma Rudolph
items.description: Track and field legend who overcame childhood polio and a corrective leg brace to become the fastest woman in the world, winning three gold medals at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

quiz.q: Wilma Rudolph is celebrated for winning how many gold medals at the 1960 Rome Olympics?
quiz.explanation: Rudolph won gold in the 100m, 200m, and 4x100m relay at the 1960 Rome Olympics, becoming the first American woman to win three gold medals at a single Olympics.

quiz.q: What serious childhood illness did Wilma Rudolph overcome on her path to becoming the world's fastest woman?
quiz.explanation: Rudolph survived polio as a child and wore a corrective brace on her left leg until age 12 — doctors told her she would never walk normally.

quiz.q: Rudolph was nicknamed 'The Tornado' and was considered what at the 1960 Olympics?
choices: The fastest woman in the world
The greatest female sprinter in history
The people's champion of the Games
quiz.explanation: Her three gold medals in Rome made her the fastest woman in the world and one of the most celebrated athletes at those Games.

quiz.q: When Rudolph returned home to Clarksville, Tennessee after her Olympic triumph, she insisted her parade do what?
choices: Be integrated — the first integrated public event in the city's history
Be held at night to include working people
March through the poorest neighborhood in the city
quiz.explanation: Rudolph refused to participate in a segregated parade, insisting it be open to both Black and white residents — making it the first integrated public event in Clarksville's history.

quiz.q: After retiring from athletics, Rudolph founded which program to help underprivileged youth through sports?
quiz.explanation: She founded the Wilma Rudolph Foundation in 1981, a nonprofit providing free coaching and academic tutoring to underprivileged children.

items.title: Zendaya Coleman
items.description: Actress, singer, and fashion icon who became the youngest person to win the Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series, beloved for her roles in Euphoria, Spider-Man, and Dune.

quiz.q: Zendaya made history at the 2020 Emmy Awards by becoming the youngest person to win what award?
choices: Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series
Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series

quiz.explanation: At age 24, Zendaya became the youngest person ever to win the Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for Euphoria (HBO).

quiz.q: Zendaya plays which complex character in the HBO drama series Euphoria?
quiz.explanation: She plays Rue Bennett, a teenager struggling with addiction, in Euphoria — a role that earned her two Emmy Awards.

quiz.q: Zendaya plays which character in the Spider-Man Marvel Cinematic Universe films?
quiz.explanation: Zendaya plays MJ, Peter Parker's love interest, in the MCU Spider-Man trilogy starring Tom Holland.

quiz.q: Zendaya starred in which epic science fiction film franchise alongside Timothée Chalamet?
quiz.explanation: She plays Chani in Denis Villeneuve's Dune (2021) and Dune: Part Two (2024), opposite Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides.

quiz.q: Before her dramatic acting career, Zendaya gained fame on which Disney Channel series?
quiz.explanation: Zendaya first became famous as Rocky Blue on Shake It Up (2010–2013), dancing alongside Bella Thorne on Disney Channel.
